claims.claim: Gundobad, 'perceiving the doctrines of the heretics to be worthless, confessed that Christ, the Son of God, and the Holy Ghost are both equal to the Father, and asked secret baptism of the holy bishop of Vienne'; Latin 'clam ut crismaretur expetiit' (asked to be anointed with chrism in secret)
claims.witness: Gregory of Tours, History of the Franks II.34, tr. Dalton (gregory-tours_history-of-the-franks-v2_dalton1927 l.3525-3533, page break at l.3530); Latin (gregory-tours_opera-mgh-srm-1-lat_arndt-krusch1885 l.7672-7676, OCR 'crismaretur', 'aequahs'); reprinted by Peiper as fragment I of the dialogues (avitus-vienne_opera-mgh-aa-6-2-lat_peiper1883 l.5461-5469)

claims.claim: The bishop's answer includes: 'Thou fearest the people, O king; but perceivest thou not that it is more meet for the people to follow thy belief, than for thee to indulge their weakness? For thou art the head of the people; the people is not thy head. If thou goest a warfare, it is thou that goest before the troops of thy host, which follow whither thou leadest.' Latin 'Tu enim es caput populi, non populus caput tuum' (OCR 'euim', 'capnt')
claims.witness: Gregory, Hist. II.34, tr. Dalton (gregory-tours_history-of-the-franks-v2_dalton1927 l.3555-3561); Latin in Peiper (avitus-vienne_opera-mgh-aa-6-2-lat_peiper1883 l.5488-5489). Gregory's report, written decades later; the words are Gregory's account of Avitus, not a text of Avitus

claims.claim: 'Though troubled by these arguments, Gundobad persisted to his dying day in this madness, nor ever would publicly confess that the three Persons of the Trinity are equal.' Gregory, a Catholic bishop, calls the king's position madness: partisan framing
claims.witness: Gregory, Hist. II.34, tr. Dalton (gregory-tours_history-of-the-franks-v2_dalton1927 l.3565-3568); Latin 'usque ad exitum vitae suae in hac insania perduravit' (avitus-vienne_opera-mgh-aa-6-2-lat_peiper1883 l.5514-5515, OCR '|)crdnravit')

claims.claim: The bishop of Vienne in this chapter is Avitus: 'The blessed Avitus was at this time of great eloquence'; Dalton's note: 'This was Avitus, whose name is mentioned farther on in the chapter'; the Latin names him 'a sancto Avito episcopo Viennense'
claims.witness: Gregory, Hist. II.34 (gregory-tours_history-of-the-franks-v2_dalton1927 l.3568, 3583; note l.24070-24071; gregory-tours_opera-mgh-srm-1-lat_arndt-krusch1885 l.7672)

claims.claim: Gregory of Tours wrote later in the same century: Brehaut, 'Gregory's life covers the years from 538 to 594'; the History 'comes down to the year 591 and the epilogue was written in 594'
claims.witness: Brehaut, introduction (gregory-tours_history-of-the-franks-selections_brehaut1916 l.81, l.430, OCR 'JGlregory'sJife', '538^0594')

claims.claim: At Gundobad's request Avitus wrote against the heresy of Eutyches (and of Sabellius, as Gregory pairs them): 'at the request of King Gundobad he wrote against them'
claims.witness: Gregory, Hist. II.34, tr. Dalton (gregory-tours_history-of-the-franks-v2_dalton1927 l.3583-3587)

claims.claim: Gregory: 'There are to-day extant among us his admirable letters, which, as they once quelled heresy, so now they edify the Church of God. He wrote a book of Homilies, six metrical books on the creation of the world and on various other subjects, and nine books of Letters'
claims.witness: Gregory, Hist. II.34, tr. Dalton (gregory-tours_history-of-the-franks-v2_dalton1927 l.3587-3592)

claims.claim: Eutyches, in Dalton's note, 'denied the orthodox doctrine as to the twofold nature of Christ, recognizing only the divine'
claims.witness: Dalton, note to II.25 (34) (gregory-tours_history-of-the-franks-v2_dalton1927 l.24084-24091, page break)

claims.claim: The Life: 'Tempore Zenonis imperatoris beatus Avitus episcopus ... Viennensem ecclesiam post patrem Isicium aeque episcopum suscepit regendam'; Isicius 'vir primum fuit senatoriae dignitatis', with two sons, 'Apollinaris Valentiae episcopus miraculis insignis et Avitus, qui ... in Viennensi episcopatu patri successor extitit' (cleaned reading). The card's 'his Life puts this in the time of the emperor Zeno' rests on 'Tempore Zenonis imperatoris'
claims.witness: Anonymous Vita Aviti, in Peiper (avitus-vienne_opera-mgh-aa-6-2-lat_peiper1883 l.18084-18090; OCR very heavy: 'Zeucniis iiuperat(UMs', ']0st ]iatreiii Isiciiiii', 'A]iolliuaris Valentiae e])iscopus niiraeulis iusignis'); hagiography

claims.claim: Ado of Vienne's Chronicle: 'Avitus quoque Viennensis episcopus ... et eius frater Apollinaris Valentiae episcopus miraculis insignis, Isicii senatorii primum viri, postea Viennensis episcopi duo lumina, clarissimi filii'. Ado names Isicius bishop of Vienne and Avitus bishop there; he does not use the word successor in these lines
claims.witness: Ado, Chronicon aet. sexta, printed by Peiper (avitus-vienne_opera-mgh-aa-6-2-lat_peiper1883 l.18098-18101, OCR 'dno lumina', 'fllii')

claims.claim: Avitus's own poem to his sister: 'Pontificem sacris adsumptum respice patrem' (look on your father, taken up into the sacred office as bishop); his brothers joined 'patrum ad consortia' in the same office
claims.witness: Avitus, Carmen VI (avitus-vienne_opera-mgh-aa-6-2-lat_peiper1883 l.26328, OCR 'pati'em'; l.26366-26367)

claims.claim: Ado of Vienne was a later (arch)bishop of Vienne: Krusch calls him 'Adone Viennensi archiepiscopo'; Peiper: 'Ado, qui mortuus est a. 874'
claims.witness: Krusch, intro to Hincmar's Vita Remigii (passiones-vitaeque-sanctorum-merovingici-mgh-srm-3-lat_krusch1896 l.19328, OCR 'archieqnscopo'); Peiper prooemium n. 28 (avitus-vienne_opera-mgh-aa-6-2-lat_peiper1883 l.1667)

claims.claim: Peiper: 'Natus videtur c. a. 460' (cf. Binding I 170 n. 564, A. Jahn II 130 sqq.); 'ipse Avitus post patrem episcopus Viennensis factus'
claims.witness: Peiper, index of persons s.v. Avitus (avitus-vienne_opera-mgh-aa-6-2-lat_peiper1883 l.30039-30041, 30058-30059)

claims.claim: Gundobad's church was Arian: the Life says Avitus fought 'adversus haeresim Arrianam ... magno sudore decertavit' and wrote a dialogue against it to Gundobad, king of the Burgundians; Ado's martyrology: 'tempore Gundobaldi regis ab infestatione Arrianae haereseos Galliae defensae sunt'; Dalton's note speaks of Avitus's homily to the king 'urging him to abandon Arianism'
claims.witness: Vita Aviti c. II (avitus-vienne_opera-mgh-aa-6-2-lat_peiper1883 l.18091-18096, OCR 'haeresini Arrianain', 'deeertavit'); Ado, Martyrology, Nones of February (avitus-vienne_opera-mgh-aa-6-2-lat_peiper1883 l.18111-18113, OCR 'snnt'); Dalton note (gregory-tours_history-of-the-franks-v2_dalton1927 l.24072-24074)

claims.claim: Letter to Clovis: heading 'Avitus episcopus Clodovecho regi' (OCR 'Clodeveclio'); 'Dum vobis eligitis, omnibus iudicatis: vestra fides nostra victoria est' (OCR 'uostra'); 'cuius ministeriis si corporaliter non accessi, gaudiorum tamen communione non defui'
claims.witness: Avitus, ep. 46 (avitus-vienne_opera-mgh-aa-6-2-lat_peiper1883 l.10305, 10313, 10331-10332)

claims.claim: The letter says the king was reborn at Christmas: 'ut consequenter eo die ad salutem regeneratrix unda vos pareret, quo natum redemptionis suae caeli dominum mundus accepit'
claims.witness: Avitus, ep. 46 (avitus-vienne_opera-mgh-aa-6-2-lat_peiper1883 l.10327-10329)

claims.claim: Peiper dates ep. 46 to Clovis 'a. 496/497'
claims.witness: Peiper, table of the letters (avitus-vienne_opera-mgh-aa-6-2-lat_peiper1883 l.43375, OCR ',, /Clodevecho» ^ /46 a. 496/497')

claims.claim: Dalton: Krusch 'maintained that the king was baptized not at Reims, but at the basilica of S. Martin at Tours in 507-8'; Dalton decides 'with Kurth, d'Arbois de Jubainville ... and L. Levillain ... that Reims must after all be retained as the place, and the year 496 as the date'; 'the rite was performed at Reims on Christmas Day'; 'none of the three early authorities who refer to the baptism mention the place'; the three are Gregory's chapter, Avitus's letter 'excusing his absence from the ceremony', and the letter of Nicetius
claims.witness: Dalton, note to II.22 (31) (gregory-tours_history-of-the-franks-v2_dalton1927 l.23893-23935)

claims.claim: Agobard of Lyon: Avitus 'cum eodem Gundobado frequenter de fide altercans, et dialogos in praesenti conficiens et epistulis absenti respondens'; he calls him 'fide catholicus, eloquentia facundissimus, ingenio acerrimus, sacrarum scripturarum expositor suavissimus, litterarum etiam saecularium doctissimus'
claims.witness: Agobard, Adversus legem Gundobadi c. 13, printed by Peiper (avitus-vienne_opera-mgh-aa-6-2-lat_peiper1883 l.5540-5547, OCR 'facuudissimus', 'couficiens')

claims.claim: Agobard wrote in the ninth century, about three centuries after Avitus: Peiper 'nono saeculo Agobardus et Florus viderunt'; 'Agobardi († 841'
claims.witness: Peiper, prooemium (avitus-vienne_opera-mgh-aa-6-2-lat_peiper1883 l.1984, l.2031)

claims.claim: Agobard: 'Qui ipso Gundobado in sua perfidia perdito successorem eius Sigismundum regem ad fidem catholicam convertit' (OCR 'Sigisraundum', 'couvertit'): he turned Gundobad's successor Sigismund to the Catholic faith 'once Gundobad was lost in his unbelief', as the brief and card render 'in sua perfidia perdito'. Whether 'perdito' means after Gundobad's death or only once he was given up as lost the words do not settle, and Peiper's date for the conversion letter falls while Gundobad lived
claims.witness: Agobard, Adversus legem Gundobadi c. 13 (avitus-vienne_opera-mgh-aa-6-2-lat_peiper1883 l.5548-5549); a ninth-century witness

claims.claim: Against Agobard's order: the letter to the pope of Rome on Sigismund's conversion, 'epistulae ad papam urbis de conversione Sigismundi regis fragmentum', which Peiper dates, with a query, 'intra a. 513 — 516?'; Peiper puts the Geneva letters and homilies 'intra annos 513 et 516', when Sigismund was proving 'fidem, quam professus erat nuper'
claims.witness: Peiper, apparatus to ep. 8 (avitus-vienne_opera-mgh-aa-6-2-lat_peiper1883 l.8102-8103, OCR 'iid piipam', 'reijis fraymentwn'); table of letters (avitus-vienne_opera-mgh-aa-6-2-lat_peiper1883 l.43290, OCR '513 — 510?'); the query is why the brief says 'tentatively'; prooemium (avitus-vienne_opera-mgh-aa-6-2-lat_peiper1883 l.3380-3383)

claims.claim: Marius of Avenches: under Florentius and Anthemius (515) 'monasterium Acauno a Sigimundo constructum est'; under Peter (516) 'rex Gundobagaudus obiit et levatus est filius eius Sigimundus rex'
claims.witness: Marius, Chronicle (chronica-minora-2_marcellinus-victor-tunnunensis-biclaro-isidore-mgh-aa-11-lat_mommsen1894 l.21181-21185, OCR 'Antheniio', 'a. 5 16'); cited by Peiper (avitus-vienne_opera-mgh-aa-6-2-lat_peiper1883 l.18289)

claims.claim: Krusch: at the founding of the monastery 'quod a. 515 Sigismundus rex in honorem martyrum Acaunensium innovaverat ... Avitus episcopus Viennensis homiliam dixit'
claims.witness: Krusch, prolegomena to the Passio Acaunensium martyrum (passiones-vitaeque-sanctorum-merovingici-mgh-srm-3-lat_krusch1896 l.2332-2334)

claims.claim: Dalton: 'Later he converted Sigismund, son of Gundobad (III. 5), to Catholicism'; 'He was converted to Catholicism by Avitus, bishop of Vienne'
claims.witness: Dalton, notes (gregory-tours_history-of-the-franks-v2_dalton1927 l.24076, l.24374-24375)

claims.claim: The Life: 'Hunc Sigismundum regem beatus Avitus post exilium in fide pietatis erudivit'
claims.witness: Vita Aviti c. V (avitus-vienne_opera-mgh-aa-6-2-lat_peiper1883 l.18280, OCR 'Sigismuudum', 'exiliuui')

claims.claim: Epaone: Avitus signs first, 'Avitus eps. constitutiones nostras id est sacerdotum provinciae Viennensis releg. et ss. d. XVII Kal. mensis octavi. Agapito conss. Epaone', ahead of 'Viventiolus eps. ecclesiae Lugdunensis' and 'Apollinaris eps. civit. Valentinae'
claims.witness: Acta of Epaone, in Peiper (avitus-vienne_opera-mgh-aa-6-2-lat_peiper1883 l.17810-17818, OCR 'saferdotum', 'Vieunensis')

claims.claim: The council is of 517: Maassen heads it 'CONCILIUM EPAONENSE A. 517.' and says its time appears from Avitus's subscription
claims.witness: Maassen (concilia-aevi-merovingici-mgh-concilia-1-lat_maassen1893 l.1945, l.2011-2013)

claims.claim: Avitus's letter of summons: 'Epistula Aviti episcopi Viennensis, qua episcopos provinciae suae invitat, ut ad concilium veniant'; 'venerabilis papae urbis nobis ob hanc neglegentiam succensentis mordacia mihi nonnumquam scripta perlata sunt'; councils 'quos bis per annum a sacerdotibus fieri cura seniorum decreverat'
claims.witness: Maassen (concilia-aevi-merovingici-mgh-concilia-1-lat_maassen1893 l.2016-2024); the same letter as ep. 90 in Peiper (avitus-vienne_opera-mgh-aa-6-2-lat_peiper1883 l.11976-11983)

claims.claim: Epaone canon 33: 'Basilicas haereticorum, quas tanta execratione habemus exosas, ut pollutionem earum purgabilem non putemus, sanctis usibus adplicare despicimus. Sane quas per violentiam nostris tulerant, possumus revocare'
claims.witness: Acta of Epaone, in Peiper (avitus-vienne_opera-mgh-aa-6-2-lat_peiper1883 l.17642-17644, OCR heavy: 'Biisilicas liaereticorum', 'desi^icimus')

claims.claim: Ep. 34, to the Roman senators Faustus and Symmachus, about the wrong done to Pope Symmachus: 'At si papa urbis vocatur in dubium, episcopatus iam videbitur, non episcopus, vacillare'; Peiper dates it 'a. 501 ex.'
claims.witness: Avitus, ep. 34 (avitus-vienne_opera-mgh-aa-6-2-lat_peiper1883 l.9609-9611, OCR 'nou', 'vaciliare'); index heading 'Fausto et Symmacho senatoribus urbis ep. XXXIIII' (avitus-vienne_opera-mgh-aa-6-2-lat_peiper1883 l.30951); Peiper's summary 'senatores urbis de iniuria Symmacho papae inlata' (avitus-vienne_opera-mgh-aa-6-2-lat_peiper1883 l.1520); table (avitus-vienne_opera-mgh-aa-6-2-lat_peiper1883 l.43351)

claims.claim: The Life: 'Moritur Anastasio adhuc principe'; Peiper's apparatus 'stasio] immo Iustino'; in the prooemium Peiper calls the Anastasius an excusable error
claims.witness: Vita Aviti c. VI (avitus-vienne_opera-mgh-aa-6-2-lat_peiper1883 l.18342, OCR 'Auastasio adbuc priuciiie'); apparatus (avitus-vienne_opera-mgh-aa-6-2-lat_peiper1883 l.18385, OCR 'iinmo lustino'); prooemium (avitus-vienne_opera-mgh-aa-6-2-lat_peiper1883 l.1641-1646)

claims.claim: Peiper's index, s.v. Avitus, after 'moritur Anastasio (immo Iustino) adhuc principe 181': 'incertum quo anno, sed post a. 525 ex. vel 526 in. quo tempore homiliam in dedicatione basilicae Genevensis dixit, ante a. 533, nam in concilio Aurelianensi Iulianus episcopus Viennensis subscripsit' (the year is uncertain, but after the end of 525 or the start of 526, when he gave the homily at the dedication of the church at Geneva, and before 533, for at the council of Orléans Julian signs as bishop of Vienne). The homily date is Binding's: 'non ante 525 ex. vel 526 in. putat Bindingius'; Peiper's prooemium puts all the Geneva letters and homilies 'intra annos 513 et 516'
claims.witness: Peiper, index of persons (avitus-vienne_opera-mgh-aa-6-2-lat_peiper1883 l.30143-30149, OCR '((wimo Iiistino)', '«.r.', 'conciUo', 'lulianus'); prooemium (l.3377-3378, OCR 'Bindiugiiis'; l.3380-3381)

claims.claim: Victor of Tunnuna enters Anastasius's death and Justin's reign under the year Mommsen heads 518: 'Anastasius imperator ... moritur' and 'Romanorum LI IVSTINVS regnavit an. VIII mens. VIIII'. With Peiper's correction of the Life's emperor to Justin ('immo Iustino', OCR 'iinmo lustino'), this is the README's ordering year, 518, which is also the Library header's
claims.witness: Victor of Tunnuna, Chronicle (chronica-minora-2_marcellinus-victor-tunnunensis-biclaro-isidore-mgh-aa-11-lat_mommsen1894 l.18560, 18562-18565, 18567); Peiper (avitus-vienne_opera-mgh-aa-6-2-lat_peiper1883 l.18385)

claims.claim: Peiper dates the latest letters 'a. 517/518' (ep. 61, to Apollinaris) and 'c. a. 518' (ep. 63)
claims.witness: Peiper, table of letters (avitus-vienne_opera-mgh-aa-6-2-lat_peiper1883 l.43417, l.43420)

claims.claim: Avitus's letters include letters to Gundobad and Sigismund, to 'papae urbis' (ep. 8), to Hormisdas (ep. 41), to 'papae Constantinopolitano' (ep. 9) and letters written in Sigismund's name to the emperor ('Sigismundus imperatori ... post m. Mart. a. 515 una cum ep. 9')
claims.witness: Peiper, table of letters (avitus-vienne_opera-mgh-aa-6-2-lat_peiper1883 l.43271-43290, 43363-43373); ep. 46 to Clovis (avitus-vienne_opera-mgh-aa-6-2-lat_peiper1883 l.10305)

claims.claim: Contra Eutychianam haeresim, two books: the Life lists 'libellos duos contra Nestorium et Eutychem' [Epp. II et III]; Peiper's table dates them 'a. 512 vel 513' and 'a. 512'
claims.witness: Vita Aviti (avitus-vienne_opera-mgh-aa-6-2-lat_peiper1883 l.18129-18130); Peiper's table (avitus-vienne_opera-mgh-aa-6-2-lat_peiper1883 l.43271-43272, OCR '5l;i', 'a. dI2')

claims.claim: Isidore of Seville, De viris illustribus 36: 'Avitus, Viennensis episcopus, scientia saecularium litterarum doctissimus edidit quinque libellos heroico metro compositos, quorum primus est de Origine mundi, secundus de Originali peccato, tertius de Essentia Dei, quartus de Diluvio mundi, quintus de Transitu maris Rubri. Scripsit et ad Fuscinam sororem de Laude virginitatis librum unum'
claims.witness: Isidore (isidore-seville_sententiae-eccl-officiis-historia-gothorum-pl83-lat_migne1860 l.122548-122556, heading 'DE VIRIS ILLUSTRIBUS LIBER' l.122187; OCR 's:ecula-', 'Uriginali', 'Trausitu')

claims.claim: His epitaph: 'Orator nullus similis nullusque poeta'
claims.witness: Epitaphium sancti Aviti, printed by Peiper (avitus-vienne_opera-mgh-aa-6-2-lat_peiper1883 heading l.18620, line l.18662, OCR 'uullus', 'uuUusque')

claims.claim: Name forms: Peiper's heading 'ALCIMI ECDICII AVITI VIENNENSIS EPISCOPI' (genitive of Alcimus Ecdicius Avitus); Agobard: 'Alcimus Avitus episcopus Viennensis'
claims.witness: Peiper (avitus-vienne_opera-mgh-aa-6-2-lat_peiper1883 l.5460, OCR 'VIENNEN8LS EPLSCOPI'); Agobard, De imaginibus c. 9 (avitus-vienne_opera-mgh-aa-6-2-lat_peiper1883 l.5524)

claims.claim: Place: Vienne under Burgundian kings: Gundobad 'Burgundionum regem' (Vita, l.18096); Epaone 'temporum Sigismundi regis' ({P} l.17051, OCR); Vienne is Gundobad's realm in Gregory II.33 (Dalton l.3498-3523)
claims.witness: avitus-vienne_opera-mgh-aa-6-2-lat_peiper1883 l.18096, l.17051; gregory-tours_history-of-the-franks-v2_dalton1927 l.3498-3523

claims.claim: The Collatio episcoporum: Peiper prints it in his appendix; it is known from 'Hieronymus Vignier in schedis manuscriptis ... ad a. 499, ex quibus collationem edidit D'Achery'; 'Codicem neque Maassenius neque ante eum Thielius investigarunt'; Peiper: it keeps 'imaginem aliquam' of the 'conloquium a. 499 habitum'. In it Avitus speaks to the king for the bishops gathered at Lyon for the feast of St Justus ('domnus Avitus ... dixit ad regem'); the note says 'Lugduni convenere'
claims.witness: Peiper (avitus-vienne_opera-mgh-aa-6-2-lat_peiper1883 l.16782-16809, 16812-16821, l.440-441, l.1903-1904; OCR heavy)

claims.claim: Peiper: the Life's chapters II-IIII 'transcripsit auctor ex vita S. Apollinaris'; Peiper holds the Life older than Ado ('Ante Adonem igitur scripta est vita') and 'eum scripsisse Gregorii tempore'; Binding called the author worthless ('prorsus nullius pretii eum dicit Bindingius') and others thought he copied Ado
claims.witness: Peiper (avitus-vienne_opera-mgh-aa-6-2-lat_peiper1883 l.18125, l.1528-1534, l.1639, l.1656-1657)

claims.claim: The Life says Avitus grieved Sigismund's killing; Peiper: 'haec non ad nostrum Avitum, sed ad cognominem abbatem Miciacensis coenobii pertinere non procul siti ab Aurelianensi urbe'. Gregory III.6 has 'the blessed abbot Avitus' plead with Chlodomer; Dalton: 'This was S. Avitus, abbot of S. Mesmin de Micy, near Orleans'. Dalton's index lists Gregory's Council-of-Paris allusion under Avitus of Vienne; not used
claims.witness: Vita (avitus-vienne_opera-mgh-aa-6-2-lat_peiper1883 l.18282); Peiper (avitus-vienne_opera-mgh-aa-6-2-lat_peiper1883 l.1648-1654); Gregory III.6, tr. Dalton (gregory-tours_history-of-the-franks-v2_dalton1927 l.4280-4283); Dalton note (gregory-tours_history-of-the-franks-v2_dalton1927 l.24412-24413); index (gregory-tours_history-of-the-franks-v2_dalton1927 l.30842-30846)

claims.claim: Ado: 'Faustus, ex abbate Lirinensis monasterii apud Regium Galliae episcopus factus ... Contra hunc scribit lucidissima fide beatissimus Avitus Viennensis episcopus'; Duchesne: 'Avit croit que le Fauste auteur de la lettre qu'il combat est Fauste le Manichéen ... Quant à l'évêque de Riez, pour lequel il professe la plus grande considération, il est, à ses yeux, hors de cause'
claims.witness: Ado, Chronicon, in Peiper (avitus-vienne_opera-mgh-aa-6-2-lat_peiper1883 l.18404-18407); Duchesne, Histoire ancienne III, note (duchesne_histoire-ancienne-de-leglise-tome3-fra_2e-ed1910 l.22585-22589)

claims.claim: Ado's martyrology keeps him on the Nones of February: 'Viennae, beati Aviti episcopi'
claims.witness: Ado, Martyrologium (avitus-vienne_opera-mgh-aa-6-2-lat_peiper1883 l.18111-18113, OCR 'Nonia Fehrumii')

claims.claim: Peiper prints Gregory II.34 as fragment I of 'DIALOGI CVM GVNDOBADO REGE VEL LIBRORVM CONTRA ARRIANOS RELIQVIAE'
claims.witness: Peiper (avitus-vienne_opera-mgh-aa-6-2-lat_peiper1883 l.5460-5464)

claims.claim: Tradition placing: Vienne in Gaul, c. 500; the census movement 'Merovingian Gallic Christianity' (480-620, Gaul) is the placing used for Gallic bishops of the period on earlier cards (Caesarius of Arles)
claims.witness: cic-website/data/world-census.json movements; era3/batch2 caesarius-of-arles.card.json

contested_claims.claim: Where and when Clovis was baptized, and so the setting of Avitus's letter
sides: O. M. Dalton, with Kurth, d'Arbois de Jubainville and Levillain: Reims, Christmas 496 (gregory-tours_history-of-the-franks-v2_dalton1927 l.23906-23925)
Bruno Krusch: the basilica of Saint Martin at Tours, 507-8 (as Dalton reports, l.23893-23900)
Peiper dates the letter 496/497 (avitus-vienne_opera-mgh-aa-6-2-lat_peiper1883 l.43375); Dalton: no early witness names the place (l.23931-23933)

contested_claims.claim: When Sigismund became Catholic
sides: Agobard of Lyon (9th c.): after Gundobad was lost in his unbelief (avitus-vienne_opera-mgh-aa-6-2-lat_peiper1883 l.5546-5547)
Vita Aviti: after an exile (l.18280)

contested_claims.claim: Under which emperor Avitus died
sides: Vita Aviti: 'Anastasio adhuc principe' (l.18342)
Peiper: 'immo Iustino', the Life in error (l.18385, l.1641-1646)
Peiper's index: no year, but after late 525 or early 526 (Binding's date for a Geneva homily) and before 533, when Julian signs as bishop of Vienne at Orléans (l.30143-30149, 3377-3381)

contested_claims.claim: The worth and date of the Vita Aviti
sides: Peiper (with A. Jahn): older than Ado, written in Gregory's time (l.1612-1614 n. 27, l.1638, l.1656-1657)

contested_claims.claim: Whether Avitus wrote against Faustus of Riez
sides: Ado of Vienne: he wrote against Faustus, bishop at Riez (l.18404-18407)

contested_claims.claim: The Collatio episcoporum before Gundobad
sides: Printed by d'Achery from Vignier's papers; no codex found by Maassen or Thiel (l.440-441, 16812-16818)
Peiper: keeps some image of a conference of 499 (l.1903-1904)

absent_details.detail: The year of Avitus's death
absent_details.note: Searched every held file that names Avitus of Vienne (Avitus/Aviti/Avito/Alcimus/Alchimus with Vienn*; grep across cic/texts .txt, whitespace-normalized, for Avit* within 250 characters of obiit/mort/died/death/decessit/excessit/starb/† and a year 500-539, in Peiper, Krusch MGH SRM 3, Maassen, Dalton, Arndt-Krusch, Duchesne, PL 65, 67, 72, 83, Mansi, Hefele, Poschmann, Isidore). That search found only the Life's 'under Anastasius', Peiper's 'rather Justin', and Peiper's letter dates (to 517/518, c. 518). Read directly, Peiper's index gives a window and no year: 'incertum quo anno, sed post a. 525 ex. vel 526 in. quo tempore homiliam in dedicatione basilicae Genevensis dixit, ante a. 533, nam in concilio Aurelianensi Iulianus episcopus Viennensis subscripsit' (l.30143-30149, OCR '«.r.', 'conciUo', 'lulianus'); the late homily date is Binding's ('non ante 525 ex. vel 526 in. putat Bindingius', l.3377-3378), which Peiper's prooemium doubts ('intra annos 513 et 516 scripsisse puto Avitum', l.3380-3381). The 'c. 450-518' in the file header is the repository's, not a source's.

absent_details.detail: The year he became bishop of Vienne

claims.claim: 'Akhs'noyo of Hierapolis had been sent into exile at Gangra; and he was imprisoned over the kitchen in the hospital there, and was suffocated by the smoke, as he states in his epistle; and at last he died'; the editors' note gives the Greek word for 'hospital' as ξενοδοχεῖον (a hostel for strangers)
claims.witness: Syriac Chronicle known as Zachariah's, VIII.5, the later compiler, tr. Hamilton and Brooks (zachariah-rhetor_chronicle_hamiltonbrooks1899 l.10225-10228; footnote 5 '£evodoxetov' l.10252, OCR for ξενοδοχεῖον; footnote marker after 'epistle;' is OCR)

claims.claim: John of Asia's list of fifty-five exiled bishops, in Bar Hebraeus: 'Philoxenum seu Xenaiam Mabugi qui Gangram in exilium missus fuit ibique supra coquinam xenodochii inclusus fumo suffocatus fuit' (sent into exile at Gangra, shut in above the kitchen of the hostel, suffocated by smoke)
claims.witness: Bar Hebraeus, Chronicon ecclesiasticum I, Latin tr. Abbeloos-Lamy (barhebraeus_chronicon-ecclesiasticum-vol1-lat_abbeloos-lamy1872 l.12146-12156, 12272-12274)

claims.claim: The same list in Michael: '(12) Philoxenus de Mabboug, qui fut envoyé à Gangres, on l'enferma au-dessus des cuisines du xenodochion, et il y fut étouffé par la fumée' (shut in above the kitchens of the hostel, choked by the smoke)
claims.witness: Michael the Syrian, Chronique, tr. Chabot (michael-the-syrian_chronique-tome2-livres-viii-xi-fra_chabot1901 l.11836-11840; OCR 'fu- mée' across the line)

claims.claim: Budge quotes Bar Hebraeus: 'sent into exile in Gangra [In Paphlagonia], and they shut him up in a room over the kitchen of a public inn, and there he was suffocated by smoke'
claims.witness: Budge, Introduction (philoxenus-of-mabbug_discourses_budge1894 l.729-733, 772)

claims.claim: An anonymous Life quoted by Assemani: 'they shut him up in an upper chamber, and made smoke in the room below it, and they shut the doors: in this way was he crowned'
claims.witness: Budge, Introduction, tr. from Assemani B.O. ii (not held) (philoxenus-of-mabbug_discourses_budge1894 l.758-768)

claims.claim: Chronicle of 846: 'post multos annos persecutionis et ipse martyrium passus est, cum inclusus fuisset in fornace ubi suffocatus est, in civitate Gangris' (after many years of persecution he too suffered martyrdom, shut in a furnace where he was suffocated, in the city of Gangra); and 'doctor magnus et martyr' (a great teacher and a martyr)
claims.witness: Chronicon ad annum 846, ed. Brooks, Latin tr. Chabot (chronica-minora-pars-prior-versio-lat_guidi1903 l.12845-12848)

claims.claim: 'Akhsenaya, later named Philoxenus, was born in the third quarter of the Vth century at a village called Tahal which was situated in Beth Garmai, probably on the confines of Persia'; the village's position is unknown (note, citing Hoffmann)
claims.witness: Budge, Introduction (philoxenus-of-mabbug_discourses_budge1894 l.399-403, 415-416; OCR 'Tahal^', 'Persia^')

claims.claim: Simeon of Beth Arsham's list of Ibas's opponents: 'Mar Xenaias ex Tahal Beth-Garmaeorum ejusque frater Addai' (Mar Xenaias of Tahal of the Beth Garmai, and his brother Addai)
claims.witness: Editors' note quoting Simeon, Bar Hebraeus II (barhebraeus_chronicon-ecclesiasticum-vol3-lat_abbeloos-lamy1877 l.3693-3698; OCR 'Belh-Garmceorum', 'Adanis'); Budge (philoxenus-of-mabbug_discourses_budge1894 l.408-410)

claims.claim: 'it is said that his name was then changed from Akhsenaya to Philoxenus'
claims.witness: Budge, Introduction (philoxenus-of-mabbug_discourses_budge1894 l.479-480)

claims.claim: Theophanes: 'Petrus autem Fullo Hierapoleos episcopum consecratum, appellaverat Philoxenum' (Peter the Fuller, having consecrated him bishop of Hierapolis, had named him Philoxenus)
claims.witness: Theophanes, Chronographia, Latin column (theophanes-confessor_chronographia-pg108-grc-lat_migne1863 l.29055-29056)

claims.claim: Evagrius: 'Xenaias, who was bishop of the neighbouring city of Hierapolis, and who was named in Greek Philoxenus'
claims.witness: Evagrius III.32, tr. Walford (evagrius-scholasticus_ecclesiastical-history_walford1846 l.6948-6950)

claims.claim: The chronicle calls him 'Akhs'noyo' throughout; the Chronicle of 846 'Philoxenus Mabbug, qui est Mar Xenaias'; Budge's title 'Philoxenus, Bishop of Mabbogh'
claims.witness: zachariah-rhetor_chronicle_hamiltonbrooks1899 l.8859, 10225; chronica-minora-pars-prior-versio-lat_guidi1903 l.12579; philoxenus-of-mabbug_discourses_budge1894 l.3

claims.claim: Philoxenus was a bishop of the church that refused Chalcedon: 'we anathematize the Council of Chalcedon also because it anathematized Nestorius, although agreeing with him and with his doctrine'; Bar Hebraeus says he 'strenue impugnavit partes Dyophysitarum' (vigorously fought the party of the two natures)
claims.witness: Philoxenus, Anathemas, tr. Budge (philoxenus-of-mabbug_discourses_budge1894 l.1090-1092); Bar Hebraeus I (barhebraeus_chronicon-ecclesiasticum-vol1-lat_abbeloos-lamy1872 l.11522-11524)

claims.claim: Peter the Fuller ordained him bishop of Mabbog or Hierapolis 'immediately after the banishment of Calandio in 485'
claims.witness: Budge, Introduction (philoxenus-of-mabbug_discourses_budge1894 l.446-449); an editor's date. The anonymous Life via Assemani gives year 800 of the Greeks, which Budge calls a mistake (l.470-476)

claims.claim: Peter was bishop of Antioch: 'ordonné métropolitain de Mabboug par Pierre d'Antioche surnommé le Foulon' (ordained metropolitan of Mabbug by Peter of Antioch, called the Fuller); Bar Hebraeus: 'Petrus ordinavit ecclesiae Mabugi sanctum Philoxenum, virum facundum et doctorem admirabilem' (an eloquent man and a wonderful teacher)
claims.witness: Michael (michael-the-syrian_chronique-tome2-livres-viii-xi-fra_chabot1901 l.10700-10705); Bar Hebraeus I (barhebraeus_chronicon-ecclesiasticum-vol1-lat_abbeloos-lamy1872 l.11518-11521; OCR 'ct')

claims.claim: Mabbug is Hierapolis: 'Bishop of Mabbogh or Hierapolis'; Evagrius 'Hierapolis'
claims.witness: Budge (philoxenus-of-mabbug_discourses_budge1894 l.448-449); Evagrius (evagrius-scholasticus_ecclesiastical-history_walford1846 l.6948)

claims.claim: Theophanes: 'Xenaias porro Satanae mancipium ... Erat is genere Persa, fortuna servus, et a proprio domino sub Calandione profugiens ... nondum baptismi lavacro expiatus, clericum se fingens' (Satan's slave ... a Persian by race, a slave by condition, fleeing his own master under Calandion ... not yet washed in baptism, passing himself off as a cleric); Peter, finding him 'baptismo nondum initiatum', decreed that ordination supplied the lack
claims.witness: Theophanes, Chronographia, Latin column (theophanes-confessor_chronographia-pg108-grc-lat_migne1863 l.28956-28959, 29052-29058; OCR 'Satanz', 'ſingens'). Hostile, Chalcedonian

claims.claim: Theophanes also calls him 'Manichaeorum sectatorem' (a follower of the Manichees) and taught that 'Domini sanctorumque imagines proscribendas et amoliendas' (the images of the Lord and saints should be banned and removed)
claims.witness: Theophanes, Latin (theophanes-confessor_chronographia-pg108-grc-lat_migne1863 l.31431, 28956-28958; OCR 'Manichzorum geclatorem'). Hostile

claims.claim: Budge reports the image charge: 'he was charged with being the author of the heresy of the breakers of the images of saints and angels'
claims.witness: Budge, Introduction (philoxenus-of-mabbug_discourses_budge1894 l.850-853)

claims.claim: The slave-and-unbaptized story 'is made both by Theodore the Reader and by Theophanes'; Budge: 'Whether Philoxenus was actually a slave ... is a matter of no consequence, but it can be proved from his own writings that he was baptized'; 'The report that Philoxenus was unbaptized is thus shown to be without foundation'
claims.witness: Budge, Introduction (philoxenus-of-mabbug_discourses_budge1894 l.483-491, 515-521, 559-560)

claims.claim: Philoxenus, letter to Zeno: 'For I was baptized in the name of Him that died'
claims.witness: Budge, Introduction (philoxenus-of-mabbug_discourses_budge1894 l.551-552; OCR quote marks at line start)

claims.claim: Theophanes is a Chalcedonian chronicler hostile to him; Budge sets 'the accounts of Theophanes, Cedrenus, Theodore Lector' against 'the doctors of his own creed'
claims.witness: Budge (philoxenus-of-mabbug_discourses_budge1894 l.883-885); Theophanes (theophanes-confessor_chronographia-pg108-grc-lat_migne1863 l.28956)

claims.claim: Ten questions to those who 'divide our Lord': 'I. If it be a demonstrable thing that Christ hath two natures, to which of them did the Virgin give birth?'
claims.witness: Philoxenus, tr. Budge (philoxenus-of-mabbug_discourses_budge1894 l.1186-1190; OCR ''^natures', 'birth.?')

claims.claim: He traced the two-natures teaching to Nestorius: the Anathemas condemn Chalcedon 'because it anathematized Nestorius, although agreeing with him'; Michael: 'il réfuta et dévoila la fausseté de la doctrine erronée des Nestoriens diophysites' (he exposed the error of the two-nature Nestorians)
claims.witness: philoxenus-of-mabbug_discourses_budge1894 l.1090-1092; Michael (michael-the-syrian_chronique-tome2-livres-viii-xi-fra_chabot1901 l.10706-10710)

claims.claim: Michael: Thomas of Harkel revised 'le livre saint de l'Évangile et tous les autres livres du Nouveau Testament ... après la première interprétation qui avait été faite à Mabboug par les soins et du temps de l'évêque Philoxenus' (after the first translation made at Mabbug through the care and in the time of bishop Philoxenus); Bar Hebraeus the same: 'post primam versionem Mabugi cura Philoxeni elaboratam'. The 'first' is the earlier version that Thomas revised, not the first Syriac New Testament ever made (Budge says the Discourses quote the Peshitta, l.2806-2819); the brief's 'a Syriac version of the New Testament was made at Mabbug through his care' and the card's 'the earlier version' rest on this
claims.witness: Michael (michael-the-syrian_chronique-tome2-livres-viii-xi-fra_chabot1901 l.29478-29486); Bar Hebraeus I (barhebraeus_chronicon-ecclesiasticum-vol1-lat_abbeloos-lamy1872 l.16120-16127). Both speak of the New Testament

claims.claim: Budge: 'a new translation of the four Gospels from Greek into Syriac ... appeared at Mabbogh in the year 508'; works list: 'A literal translation of the Old and New Testaments which was completed about A. D. 508. This great work was completed with the assistance of the chorepiscopus, Polycarp'
claims.witness: Budge (philoxenus-of-mabbug_discourses_budge1894 l.874-881, 1721-1724); Polycarp in no ancient held line (searched polycarp/Polycarpus in MICH, BH1, BH3, PSZ)

claims.claim: 'In the year 498 Flavian II. ascended the episcopal throne of Antioch ... he made Philoxenus a bitter and implacable enemy who gave him no rest until he succeeded in effecting his deposition in 512'
claims.witness: Budge (philoxenus-of-mabbug_discourses_budge1894 l.594-600)

claims.claim: The Synod at Sidon met in 'the eight hundred and twenty-third year of the Greeks'; editors' note '512'; Philoxenus 'exposed Calandion of Antioch, and ejected him from his See'; Flavian: 'lest we should arouse the sleeping dragon'
claims.witness: zachariah-rhetor_chronicle_hamiltonbrooks1899 VII.10 l.8851-8866, 8885-8888 (note 3 '512')

claims.claim: 'But the zeal of Akhs'noyo urged the monks again ... they assembled at Antioch against him. And some of them were wounded, and others were killed; but nevertheless Flavian was ejected from his See'
claims.witness: zachariah-rhetor_chronicle_hamiltonbrooks1899 VII.10 l.8895-8901. Friendly witness, from his own side, as the brief and card mark it

claims.claim: Evagrius, from aged men who remembered: the monks, 'having been wrought upon by Xenaias ... rushed into the city in a body'; 'the people of the city made a great slaughter of them, so that a very large number found a grave in the Orontes'
claims.witness: Evagrius III.32, tr. Walford (evagrius-scholasticus_ecclesiastical-history_walford1846 l.6944-6956). Chalcedonian witness

claims.claim: Evagrius writes for Chalcedon's side (already established in the approved Evagrius Scholasticus card, batch 5)
claims.witness: evagrius-scholasticus_ecclesiastical-history_walford1846 l.1222-1236

claims.claim: Chronicle of 846: 'Episcopi autem qui eius ordinationem fecerunt hi sunt: Dionysius Tarsi; Philoxenus Mabbug, qui est Mar Xenaias' (the bishops who ordained Severus: ... Philoxenus of Mabbug, who is Mar Xenaias)
claims.witness: chronica-minora-pars-prior-versio-lat_guidi1903 l.12578-12580

claims.claim: 'in the second year of the reign of Justin, which was An. 830, he thrust out of Antioch Severus, and Xenaias from Mabug, and everybody that received not the four synods'; Budge reads 830 as 'A.D. 518 — 519'. The 'he' is Justin, and the brief's 'the emperor Justin ... drove Severus from Antioch and Philoxenus from Mabbug' gives Xenaias the brief's one name for him
claims.witness: Chronicle of Edessa, tr. Cowper (chronicle-of-edessa_cowper l.217); Latin in chronica-minora-pars-prior-versio-lat_guidi1903 l.1261-1262; Budge (philoxenus-of-mabbug_discourses_budge1894 l.722-724)

claims.claim: 'From a letter which Philoxenus wrote to the monks of the monastery of Senun near Edessa in 522 we learn that his first place of banishment was Philippopolis in Thrace; in the following year he was sent into exile in Gangra'
claims.witness: Budge (philoxenus-of-mabbug_discourses_budge1894 l.727-731; OCR 'Philippo- polls'); the letter is not held

claims.claim: Budge's list of works calls the Senun letter 'written during his second exile at Philippopolis'
claims.witness: Budge (philoxenus-of-mabbug_discourses_budge1894 l.2160-2161)

claims.claim: Nau: 'Philoxène (Xénaïas), évêque de Mabboug, de 485 à 523'
claims.witness: F. Nau, Textes monophysites, Introduction, PO 13 (chronicle-of-seert_histoire-nestorienne-seconde-partie-po13-ara-fra_scher1919 l.10503-10504; Nau signs the fascicle, l.77-86, 8103). An editor's years

claims.claim: Budge's title page: 'The Discourses of Philoxenus, Bishop of Mabbogh, A.D. 485-519'
claims.witness: philoxenus-of-mabbug_discourses_budge1894 l.3

claims.claim: Palestinian monks to Alcison, as Evagrius quotes them: 'Xenaias, who was truly a stranger to God'
claims.witness: Evagrius III.31, heading 'LETTER TO ALCISON FROM THE MONKS OF PALESTINE' (evagrius-scholasticus_ecclesiastical-history_walford1846 l.6776-6799); Budge wrongly gives the words to Evagrius himself (l.798-799)

claims.claim: 'Faith is the foundation and the architect'
claims.witness: Philoxenus, Discourses, tr. Budge (philoxenus-of-mabbug_discourses_budge1894 l.12638)

claims.claim: Thirteen Discourses: on faith (2-3), simplicity (4-5), the fear of God (6-7), poverty (8-9), the lust of the belly (10), abstinence (11), fornication (12-13), by Budge's headings
Budge: written 'some years after 485 ... and before the close of the Vth century', since 'all the quotations are taken from the Peshitta'
claims.witness: Budge (philoxenus-of-mabbug_discourses_budge1894 l.2806-2819)

claims.claim: About ten British Museum manuscripts rank 'the authority of Philoxenus, on matters of doctrine' as 'equal to that of Severus of Antioch, Isaac of Antioch, Cyril of Alexandria, Chrysostom, Ephraim the Syrian'
claims.witness: Budge (philoxenus-of-mabbug_discourses_budge1894 l.886-894; OCR 'ten^')

claims.claim: Dionysius bar Salibi, 'the star among the Jacobites of the XIIth century', bishop of Mar'ash, Mabbogh and Amid, gives the opinions of the 'true and orthodox doctors and holy fathers like Severus the Great ... and Philoxenus of Mabbogh'
claims.witness: Budge (philoxenus-of-mabbug_discourses_budge1894 l.895-922)

claims.claim: Bar Hebraeus: Philoxenus 'minor', nephew of Philoxenus of Mabbug by his sister, 'mortuo in Gangra avunculo suo, ob causam quam tacitus praetermitto, consensit synodo Chalcedonensi et vixit in Cypro'; Michael: 'Philoxenus, fils de sa sœur, pour un motif que je m'abstiens d'écrire, adhéra au [Synode] et devint évêque en Cypre'
claims.witness: Bar Hebraeus I (barhebraeus_chronicon-ecclesiasticum-vol1-lat_abbeloos-lamy1872 l.13257-13262; OCR 'Midmgensis', 'ol> cau-'); Michael (michael-the-syrian_chronique-tome2-livres-viii-xi-fra_chabot1901 l.18300-18304)

claims.claim: Severus to Julian of Halicarnassus: 'I once and again examined the teaching of the memorable Akhs'noyo and Eleusinus the bishops'
claims.witness: zachariah-rhetor_chronicle_hamiltonbrooks1899 IX.13, the response of Severus to Julian (heading l.11753-11754; quote l.12068-12069)

claims.claim: Budge: 'energetic and fiery' (quoting Wright) and 'a merciless and relentless opponent of all such as differed from him in their opinions on the natures of Christ'; 'a final decision as to his behaviour and character cannot be arrived at until the case is stated from the point of view of Philoxenus'
claims.witness: Budge (philoxenus-of-mabbug_discourses_budge1894 l.774-790)

claims.claim: Calandio expelled him 'between the years 481 and 485 ... as a preacher of the views of Cyril of Alexandria'; Theophanes: 'Et Calandion quidem exterminaverat' (Calandion had driven him out)
claims.witness: Budge (philoxenus-of-mabbug_discourses_budge1894 l.441-445); Theophanes (theophanes-confessor_chronographia-pg108-grc-lat_migne1863 l.29053-29054)

claims.claim: Michael: 'Il dévoila Cala[n]dion d'Antioche' (he exposed Calandion of Antioch)
claims.witness: Michael (michael-the-syrian_chronique-tome2-livres-viii-xi-fra_chabot1901 l.11090-11091)

claims.claim: Budge: came to Edessa 'probably in his early manhood, where he studied'
claims.witness: Budge (philoxenus-of-mabbug_discourses_budge1894 l.411-414)

claims.claim: Chronicle of 846: 'olim fuerat unus e ducibus scholae quae antea erat in urbe Edessa ... ei inviderunt, et eum expulerunt ab omni schola ... quia non consensit cum eis doctrinae Nestorii' (he had been one of the leaders of the school at Edessa; they envied him and drove him out because he did not agree with them in the teaching of Nestorius)
claims.witness: chronica-minora-pars-prior-versio-lat_guidi1903 l.12556-12563; OCR 'Nestorn'

claims.claim: Bar Hebraeus: the Persian teachers 'Edessa expulsi fuere opera Philoxeni seu Xenaiae Mabugensis, qui pariter genere Persa erat' (were driven from Edessa through the efforts of Philoxenus or Xenaias of Mabbug, also a Persian)
claims.witness: Bar Hebraeus II (barhebraeus_chronicon-ecclesiasticum-vol3-lat_abbeloos-lamy1877 l.3249-3253; OCR 'cxpulsi', 'Mabngensis')

contested_claims.claim: How and when he died at Gangra
contested_claims.sides: Smoke over the hostel kitchen: the chronicle known as Zachariah's VIII.5, adding that he wrote of it in a letter and 'at last he died' (zachariah-rhetor_chronicle_hamiltonbrooks1899 l.10225-10228); John of Asia's list in Bar Hebraeus (barhebraeus_chronicon-ecclesiasticum-vol1-lat_abbeloos-lamy1872 l.12146-12156, 12272-12274) and Michael (michael-the-syrian_chronique-tome2-livres-viii-xi-fra_chabot1901 l.11836-11840). Smoke made on purpose below a locked upper room: the anonymous Life via Assemani, quoted by Budge (philoxenus-of-mabbug_discourses_budge1894 l.758-768). Shut in a furnace, after many years of persecution: the Chronicle of 846 (chronica-minora-pars-prior-versio-lat_guidi1903 l.12845-12848). Year: Nau 523 as the end of his time as bishop (PO 13 l.10503-10504); Budge, the year after 522 for the move to Gangra (l.727-731) and 485-519 on his title page (l.3).

contested_claims.claim: Whether he was a runaway slave and unbaptized when made bishop
contested_claims.sides: Theophanes (theophanes-confessor_chronographia-pg108-grc-lat_migne1863 l.28956-29058) and Theodore the Reader, as Budge reports (l.483-491), say yes; Budge answers from Philoxenus's own words on his baptism and calls the slavery question of no consequence (l.515-560).

contested_claims.claim: Who drove out whom under Calandion
contested_claims.sides: Theophanes (theophanes-confessor_chronographia-pg108-grc-lat_migne1863 l.29053-29054) and Budge (l.441-445): Calandion expelled Philoxenus. contested_claims.claim: How and where Boethius was put to death
contested_claims.sides: Anonymus Valesianus: cord twisted on the forehead, then clubbed, 'in agro Calventiano' (prosper_chronica-minora-1-lat_mommsen1892 l.41429-41432). Book of the Popes: with the sword, bodies concealed (liber-pontificalis_book-of-the-popes-v1_loomis1916 l.10496-10507). Agnellus: Symmachus and Boethius beheaded with axes (prosper_chronica-minora-1-lat_mommsen1892 l.42064-42067). Marius: 'in territorio Mediolanense' (chronica-minora-2_marcellinus-victor-tunnunensis-biclaro-isidore-mgh-aa-11-lat_mommsen1894 l.21310). Stewart and Rand: imprisoned at Pavia (boethius_theological-tractates-consolation_stewart-rand1918 l.250). The Bollandists report one writer's doubt of the AV account, since others say the sword, and answer that the sword is not in Procopius (acta-sanctorum_maii-tomus-6-lat_1739 l.16339-16343; reading reconstructed from heavy OCR).

contested_claims.claim: Whether the theological tractates, and the fourth in particular, are his
contested_claims.sides: Against: scholars reported by Hodgkin (cassiodorus_variae-letters-hodgkin1886 l.3984-3988); Jourdain's Boethus (l.4008-4012); Hodgkin on Tr. IV (l.3974-3978). For: the Anecdoton, which Hodgkin says is a later excerpt of a Cassiodorus tract (l.3741-3742, 3757-3770); Hodgkin for I-III and V (l.4027-4030); Stewart and Rand for all five (boethius_theological-tractates-consolation_stewart-rand1918 l.322-336, 2711-2719).

contested_claims.claim: Whether he died a Christian, and whether he is a martyr
contested_claims.sides: Hodgkin: Christ never named in the Consolation, a theist's tone, yet professing Christian in full communion (cassiodorus_variae-letters-hodgkin1886 l.3999-4000, 4054-4058). Stewart and Rand: 'without doubt a Christian, a Doctor and perhaps a martyr' (boethius_theological-tractates-consolation_stewart-rand1918 l.336-337). The Bollandists list him as a martyr at Pavia (acta-sanctorum_maii-tomus-6-lat_1739 l.8153-8155), and cite Ferrarius's two catalogs, of the saints of Italy and of saints 'qui non sunt in Martyrologio Romano', both naming him a martyr at Pavia, the second under Theodoric (l.16492-16497; reading reconstructed from heavy OCR). No ancient held text calls him a martyr.

contested_claims.claim: Whether his death came before or during Pope John I's embassy to Constantinople
contested_claims.sides: Book of the Popes: during John's absence (liber-pontificalis_book-of-the-popes-v1_loomis1916 l.10490-10507). Anonymus Valesianus: before the king sends for John (c. 87-88, prosper_chronica-minora-1-lat_mommsen1892 l.41426-41435). Loomis's note (l.10538-10545) summarizes the AV and a third chronicle, with an error ('strangled'; 'father-in-law (Boethius)'), so it is not used.

contested_claims.claim: Whether Cassiodorus sided with the accusers
contested_claims.sides: Hodgkin reads Var. viii.16 to Opilio as leaning toward the accusers (cassiodorus_variae-letters-hodgkin1886 l.15285-15306). The Anecdoton, from a Cassiodorus tract, praises Boethius (cassiodorus_variae-letters-hodgkin1886 l.3738-3746). Boethius's own account calls his accusers 'vile and base' (boethius_theological-tractates-consolation_stewart-rand1918 l.7104-7105).

absent_details.detail: His birth year and place in an ancient source
absent_details.note: Searched the 205 held files that name him (boethi, boetius, boetii, boetio; 'anicius manlius'; born/natus/geboren/né near the name): only Stewart and Rand (l.240-241), Hodgkin (l.3904-3909) and Robinson (eugippius file l.2550). Ennodius's Paraenesis, Hodgkin's chief basis, is not held.

absent_details.detail: Any ancient source calling him a martyr or saint
absent_details.note: Searched 'martyr|mattyi|manyris' within 80 characters of boethius/boetius/boetii/boethii/boctio across cic/texts: no hit, since the Bollandist lines are too corrupt for the pattern; read directly, only the Bollandists' own list (1739, l.8153-8155) and Ferrarius's two catalogs that they cite, of the saints of Italy and of saints not in the Roman Martyrology (l.16492-16497) call him martyr. Procopius, the AV, the Book of the Popes, Marius and Agnellus say nothing of martyrdom.

absent_details.detail: Names of his father and sons in an ancient narrative
absent_details.note: The consular lists give a Boethius for 487 and Symmachus and Boethius for 522 without kinship; Boethius names neither; Hodgkin supplies both (l.3909-3910, 3924).

absent_details.detail: Any English of the Anonymus Valesianus, Marius or Agnellus
absent_details.note: None held; the brief and card tell them in modern words and quote no English from them.

absent_details.detail: The day of his death and his burial place
absent_details.note: No held ancient line gives a day. The Bollandist feast passage is unreadable (l.16486-16488). Searched 'ciel d'oro', 'coelo aureo', 'cielo d'oro': no hit for Boethius.

claims.claim: An Arian priest 'in fundo Gabardilla', in the territory of Sicca ('In territorio denique Siccensi'), 'cui nomen quidem fuit inter homines Felix', 'natione barbarus', had the two monks seized on the roads and ordered them beaten ('inferri praecepit verbera')
claims.witness: The Life of Fulgentius, by a disciple, PL 65, ch. 10 (fulgentius-ruspe_opera-contra-arianos-pl65-lat_migne1847 l.8403-8423; two-column OCR, the passage read across alternate half-lines; OCR 'pres- ovter', 'Gabardilla per- fidiam')

claims.claim: Abbot Felix: 'Parcite, ait, fratri Fulgenlio [OCR], qui nou [OCR] potest tormenta perferre ... Convertatur in me vestra crudelitas'; the priest has Felix beaten first
claims.witness: The Life of Fulgentius, by a disciple, PL 65, ch. 10 §19 (fulgentius-ruspe_opera-contra-arianos-pl65-lat_migne1847 l.8413-8425)

claims.claim: Fulgentius, 'vir omnino delicati corporis', is beaten, gets a pause by telling the story of his journey, and is beaten again ('Caedite, ait, iterum fortiter'); the narrator has the pain from Fulgentius himself: 'sicut ipse nobis postea referebat'
claims.witness: The Life of Fulgentius, by a disciple, PL 65, ch. 11 §20 (fulgentius-ruspe_opera-contra-arianos-pl65-lat_migne1847 l.8496-8560, read across columns)

claims.claim: The priest threw them out shaved and naked: 'deformiter decalvatos, ablatis etiam omnibus vestimentis, ex domo sua nudos inanesque projecit'
claims.witness: The Life of Fulgentius, by a disciple, PL 65, ch. 11 §21 (fulgentius-ruspe_opera-contra-arianos-pl65-lat_migne1847 l.8571-8573)

claims.claim: 'Arianorum episcopus', who knew his parents, was angry with the priest 'suae religionis et parochiae' and offered to avenge him; Fulgentius: 'Non licet, ait, in hoc saeculo vindictam quaerere [OCR "qu:e- rere"] Christiano'
claims.witness: The Life of Fulgentius, by a disciple, PL 65, ch. 11 §22 (fulgentius-ruspe_opera-contra-arianos-pl65-lat_migne1847 l.8485-8515, right column)

claims.claim: The Life is headed 'S. Fulgentii episcopi Ruspensis Vita, a quodam ejus discipulo conscripta, ad Felicianum episcopum sancti Fulgentii successorem'; its author was raised with Felicianus under Fulgentius ('a quo simul nutriti sumus') and became a monk 'in illo parvissimo monasterio quod sibi apud Sardiniam ... effecerat', living 'ante eum positus'; he tells 'omnia quae memoriter nobis audientibus ipse referebat'. The brief's 'by a Catholic monk who lived with him, tells this from what Fulgentius told him' rests on this, on 'sicut ipse nobis postea referebat' in the beating story (l.8501), and on the Life's Catholic side against the Arian king (ch. 21-22)
claims.witness: The Life of Fulgentius, by a disciple, PL 65, title and prologue (fulgentius-ruspe_opera-contra-arianos-pl65-lat_migne1847 l.7909-7914, 7935, 7992-7999 col., 8003-8004)

claims.claim: Note (a) to the Life: P. Chifflet and others think it is by Ferrandus, deacon of Carthage, for reasons in his preface to Ferrandus's works, Dijon 1649 ('Divione edita anno 1649'); 'Alios tamen haec [OCR hx] non convincunt, cum Vitae auctor videatur a latere Fulgentii non discessisse, nec id de Ferrando possit affirmari. V. Bolland.'. Note (b): 'in Vita a Chiffl. edita inter opera Ferrandi' (OCR 'iutcr'), so Chifflet edited the Life with Ferrandus's works. The brief's 'P. Chifflet, editor of Ferrandus in 1649' rests on note (a), 'praefatione ad opera Fulgentii Ferrandi Divione edita anno 1649', and on note (b)
claims.witness: Notes (a) and (b) in Migne's edition of the Life (fulgentius-ruspe_opera-contra-arianos-pl65-lat_migne1847 l.7961-7967, 7969-7970); matches the approved Ferrandus profile (era3/batch2)

claims.claim: Gallandi takes the Life to be Ferrandus's ('Ferrandi, ut censeo, genuinum opus'), lists Pithou, Miraeus, Christianus Lupus and Natalis Alexander for it, and Noris, Pagi, Mangeant and Fontanini against
claims.witness: Gallandi, Notitia on Ferrandus, PL 67 (facundus-ferrandus-caesarius-dionysius-pl67-lat_migne1865 l.68661, 68670-68682)

claims.claim: His parents were of the senators of Carthage ('parentes habuit ex numero [OCR munero] Carthaginensium senatorum'); his grandfather Gordianus left for Italy under Geiseric; two sons returned and went to Byzacium, and 'in Tellepte civitate ... Claudius, ex conjuge nomine Mariana ... feliciter genuit'
claims.witness: The Life of Fulgentius, by a disciple, PL 65, ch. 1 §4 (fulgentius-ruspe_opera-contra-arianos-pl65-lat_migne1847 l.8041-8061, read across columns)

claims.claim: Thelepte was the birthplace of Fulgentius ('Thelepte a été la patrie de saint Fulgence, évêque de Ruspe'); Thelepte is a town of Byzacena
claims.witness: Joseph Mesnage, L'Afrique chrétienne (mesnage_afrique-chretienne-eveches-ruines-antiques-fra_1912 l.8121; Byzacena fortresses incl. Thelepte l.4401)

claims.claim: He was made procurator, a tax post: chapter heading 'Procurator ordinatur'; he was ordered to be harsh 'in exigendis pensionibus' and tired of worldly business
claims.witness: The Life of Fulgentius, by a disciple, PL 65, ch. 1-2 (fulgentius-ruspe_opera-contra-arianos-pl65-lat_migne1847 l.8013-8014, 8048-8052 right col.)

claims.claim: He was moved to make his vow public 'beati Augustini exponentis tricesimum sextum psalmum disputatione commonitus et compunctus'. The Augustine is the bishop of Hippo, whom Fulgentius himself names 'Augustinum Hipponensem' (De veritate praedestinationis II, l.42467); hence the brief's and card's 'Augustine of Hippo'
claims.witness: The Life of Fulgentius, by a disciple, PL 65, ch. 3 (fulgentius-ruspe_opera-contra-arianos-pl65-lat_migne1847 l.8192-8194)

claims.claim: His mother ran to the monastery of Bishop Faustus: 'Redde, inquiens, filium matri, redde dominum servis'; she wailed 'magnis ante januam monasterii clamoribus', calling Fulgentius's name
claims.witness: The Life of Fulgentius, by a disciple, PL 65, ch. 5 (fulgentius-ruspe_opera-contra-arianos-pl65-lat_migne1847 l.8221-8222 right col., 8257-8259)

claims.claim: The Faustus who first took him in was a Catholic bishop relegated near his own see under Huneric, who had built a monastery there ('Fuit autem tunc temporis episcopus quidam ... nomine Faustus, qui pro fide catholica non longe a cathedra sua jussus fuerat relegari')
claims.witness: The Life of Fulgentius, by a disciple, PL 65, ch. 4 §9 (fulgentius-ruspe_opera-contra-arianos-pl65-lat_migne1847 l.8205-8222 left col.)

claims.claim: Reading the lives and Conferences of the Egyptian monks he sailed from Carthage with one brother, Redemptus, 'Alexandriam petiturus'; at Syracuse Bishop Eulalius told him the lands he sought 'a communione beati Petri perfida dissensio separavit' and sent him back; Bishop Rufinianus advised the same
claims.witness: The Life of Fulgentius, by a disciple, PL 65, ch. 12-13 (fulgentius-ruspe_opera-contra-arianos-pl65-lat_migne1847 l.8580-8590, 8700-8720, read across columns)

claims.claim: At Rome there was great joy 'Theoderici regis praesentia'; at the place called Palma Aurea, 'memorato Theoderico rege concionem faciente', he saw the Roman curia and heard the people's applause, and said: 'Fratres, Quam speciosa potest esse Hierusalem coelestis, si sic fulget Roma terrestris!'
claims.witness: The Life of Fulgentius, by a disciple, PL 65, ch. 13 §27 (fulgentius-ruspe_opera-contra-arianos-pl65-lat_migne1847 l.8712-8728 right col., 8778-8779); for 'Theodoric, the Ostrogothic king': Dalton's note, 'Theodoric the Great, king of the Ostrogoths' (gregory-tours_history-of-the-franks-v2_dalton1927 l.23889-23890)

claims.claim: The king had forbidden the ordination of bishops ('regalis auctoritas episcopos ordinari prohibuerat'); the remaining bishops resolved to ordain 'adversus praeceptum regis'; Fulgentius hid; then the people of Ruspe, with the leave of the primate Victor, seized him in his cell 'dolens oculos': 'pontifex esse non rogatur, sed cogitur'
claims.witness: The Life of Fulgentius, by a disciple, PL 65, ch. 16-17 (fulgentius-ruspe_opera-contra-arianos-pl65-lat_migne1847 l.8984-9038, read across columns)

claims.claim: He was taken into exile in Sardinia with the others: 'Interea repente diriguntur ministri regalis furoris, ut detentus etiam ipse cum caeteris in exsilium Sardiniam ... truderetur'
claims.witness: The Life of Fulgentius, by a disciple, PL 65, ch. 20 §40 (fulgentius-ruspe_opera-contra-arianos-pl65-lat_migne1847 l.9211-9213)

claims.claim: Thrasamund 'catholicos insectatur, catholicorum ecclesias claudit et Sardiniam exilio omni Africana ecclesia CXX episcopos mittit'; 'Eo tempore Fulgentius Ruspensis civitatis episcopus in nostro dogmate claruit' (OCR 'cxilio', 'ccclesia', 'Fulgcntius')
claims.witness: Victor of Tunnuna, Chronicle (chronica-minora-2_marcellinus-victor-tunnunensis-biclaro-isidore-mgh-aa-11-lat_mommsen1894 l.18318-18323); Isidore, Historia Vandalorum 81, same count 'cxx episcopos' (isidore-seville_sententiae-eccl-officiis-historia-gothorum-pl83-lat_migne1860 l.120075-120079); both write from the Catholic side ('in nostro dogmate')

claims.claim: The English Life of 1605 says 'the King exiled threescore Bishops and more into Sard[inia]' (long s in the OCR: 'threeſcore Biſhops'); Schaff says he 'with sixty catholic bishops of Africa was banished'
claims.witness: Anonymous English abridged Life, 1605 (victor-of-vita_memorable-and-tragical-history-persecution-eng_1605 l.8919-8921, OCR rough); Philip Schaff (npnf101_augustine-confessions-letters l.1420)

claims.claim: Thrasamund, asking who could defend the Catholic doctrine, was told of Fulgentius among the exiled bishops, and summoned him ('servum strenuum celeriter' sent); Fulgentius came to Carthage, where the number of the wise grew 'apud Carthaginem'
claims.witness: The Life of Fulgentius, by a disciple, PL 65, ch. 21 §44-45 (fulgentius-ruspe_opera-contra-arianos-pl65-lat_migne1847 l.9362-9390, 9405-9411)

claims.claim: The king sent him 'Dicta ... veneno perfidiae plena'; he divided them 'per objectionum capitula' and set brief answers under each; the king 'quia nunquam praedestinatus fuerat ad salutem, laudat sapientiam, miratur eloquentiam, praedicat humilitatem, neque tamen meretur intelligere [OCR inlelligero] veritatem'
claims.witness: The Life of Fulgentius, by a disciple, PL 65, ch. 22 §46 (fulgentius-ruspe_opera-contra-arianos-pl65-lat_migne1847 l.9421-9436); partisan: the Life's own judgement of the king

claims.claim: Contra Arianos prints the king's statements as numbered objections, each with Fulgentius's answer; the first answer: 'Haec responsione non indigent, quia fidei nostrae concordant'
claims.witness: Fulgentius, Contra Arianos liber unus (fulgentius-ruspe_opera-contra-arianos-pl65-lat_migne1847 l.13624-13640, heading OCR 'LIBBR', 'OBJECTJOtfES DEGE*')

claims.claim: The king had a second set of questions read to him once only ('interrogationem suam semel tantum beato Fulgentio praecepit legi'); he answered in three books ('tres libellos mirabiles facit')
claims.witness: The Life of Fulgentius, by a disciple, PL 65, ch. 23 §47 (fulgentius-ruspe_opera-contra-arianos-pl65-lat_migne1847 l.9460-9479); Ad Trasimundum heading (fulgentius-ruspe_opera-contra-arianos-pl65-lat_migne1847 l.14737)

claims.claim: To the king: the king refused him even one night to read the book ('noctis unius nobis spatium fuisset indultum; quod ... omnino statuit abnegandum'); 'apud eos qui Christianae gratiae participatione redempti sunt, pene id esse, fidem nolle asserere, quod negare'
claims.witness: Fulgentius, Ad Trasimundum I.1-2 (fulgentius-ruspe_opera-contra-arianos-pl65-lat_migne1847 l.14765-14783)

claims.claim: Arian partisans told the king 'Sine causa, rex, laboras ... nisi cito subveneris, religio nostra deficiet'; 'Suggerentibus talia rex ... beatum Fulgentium rursum ad exsilium Sardiniae revocare compellit' (OCR 'rur* 8om', 'Sardini*')
claims.witness: The Life of Fulgentius, by a disciple, PL 65, ch. 24-25 §48-49 (fulgentius-ruspe_opera-contra-arianos-pl65-lat_migne1847 l.9506-9525 left col., 9452-9456 right col.)

claims.claim: 'Mors enim Trasamundi regis, et mirabilis bonitas Hilderici regnare incipientis' restored the Church's freedom and gave Carthage its own bishop; on his return 'silens multitudo super littus staret' looking for him among the bishops; he was presented to 'sanctae memoriae Bonifacio episcopo'
claims.witness: The Life of Fulgentius, by a disciple, PL 65, ch. 28-29 (fulgentius-ruspe_opera-contra-arianos-pl65-lat_migne1847 l.9711-9716, 9751-9780)

claims.claim: Hilderic ordered the Catholic priests to return from exile and the churches to open; Thrasamund's death is under 'Maximo v. c. cons.', which Mommsen's margin gives as 523
claims.witness: Victor of Tunnuna (chronica-minora-2_marcellinus-victor-tunnunensis-biclaro-isidore-mgh-aa-11-lat_mommsen1894 l.18609-18611, 18636-18642); the year 523 is Mommsen's

claims.claim: Hilderic ends the persecution 'En 523'
claims.witness: Joseph Mesnage (mesnage_afrique-chretienne-eveches-ruines-antiques-fra_1912 l.1494-1495)

claims.claim: 'Trasimundi morte, quae anno 525 contigit' (OCR 'Trasifflundi'); in these Migne prints 3 is often read as 5, so the figure may be 523
claims.witness: Unsigned prolegomena to Fulgentius, PL 65 (fulgentius-ruspe_opera-contra-arianos-pl65-lat_migne1847 l.7446-7447)

claims.claim: The prolegomena: 'Augustini discipulum scias, non magis ex consensione dogmatum quam ex similitudine virtutum'; the prefacer writes at the request of the edition's editors ('mihi eorum qui editioni praefuerunt rogatu aliquid ... praefaturo') and names no author
claims.witness: Unsigned preface to Fulgentius's works, PL 65 (fulgentius-ruspe_opera-contra-arianos-pl65-lat_migne1847 l.7083-7084, 7139-7141)

claims.claim: Faustus 'episcopus Galliarum' wrote two books against grace; 'Quibus ... septem libris [Fulgentius] respondit'
claims.witness: The Life of Fulgentius, by a disciple, PL 65, ch. 28 (fulgentius-ruspe_opera-contra-arianos-pl65-lat_migne1847 l.9686-9697, read across columns)

claims.claim: 'adversus duos libros Fausti Galli septem libros edidit'
claims.witness: Letter XV of the African bishops exiled in Sardinia to John and Venerius (fulgentius-ruspe_opera-contra-arianos-pl65-lat_migne1847 l.28904-28905)

claims.claim: Isidore lists 'de gratia Dei et libero arbitrio libros responsionum septem, in quibus Fausto, Galliae Regiensis urbis episcopo ... respondens'
claims.witness: Isidore, De viris illustribus 27 (isidore-seville_sententiae-eccl-officiis-historia-gothorum-pl83-lat_migne1860 l.122088-122092; OCR 'Galli&')

claims.claim: Faustus Gallus 'a sanctae memoriae Fulgentio Ruspensi detectus atque convictus est'. Facundus names no seven books; the card says only that he says Faustus was exposed and refuted by Fulgentius
claims.witness: Facundus of Hermiane, Pro defensione trium capitulorum (facundus-ferrandus-caesarius-dionysius-pl67-lat_migne1865 l.66179-66183, OCR 'memoriz', 'de- tectus')

claims.claim: The seven books against Faustus are lost: 'Septem libros edidit ... qui nunc deperditi sunt'
claims.witness: August Engelbrecht, preface to Faustus of Riez (faustus-riez_de-gratia-and-collected-works_engelbrecht1891 l.622-628)

claims.claim: To Monimus: addressed 'fili carissime Monime' and 'Monime carissime'; the prolegomena: 'Erat is ex praecipuis ejus amicis'
claims.witness: Ad Monimum I.1 (fulgentius-ruspe_opera-contra-arianos-pl65-lat_migne1847 l.10155; l.11500); prolegomena (fulgentius-ruspe_opera-contra-arianos-pl65-lat_migne1847 l.7139-7141)

claims.claim: 'Proinde potuit, sicut voluit, praedestinare quosdam ad gloriam, quosdam ad poenam. Sed quos praedestinavit ad gloriam, praedestinavit ad justitiam. Quos autem praedestinavit ad poenam, non praedestinavit ad culpam'; also 'ad poenam debitam, non ad malum faciendum, posse dici aliam praedestinationem'
claims.witness: Ad Monimum I (fulgentius-ruspe_opera-contra-arianos-pl65-lat_migne1847 l.10644-10647; l.10265-10268 col.)

claims.claim: After the exile he wrote 'decem libros Fabiani ... de veritate praedestinationis et gratiae libellos tres'
claims.witness: The Life of Fulgentius, by a disciple, PL 65, ch. 29 (fulgentius-ruspe_opera-contra-arianos-pl65-lat_migne1847 l.9929-9932; OCR 'prxdestinationia ct gratix')

claims.claim: De veritate praedestinationis printed in three books
claims.witness: PL 65 running heads LIB. I-III (fulgentius-ruspe_opera-contra-arianos-pl65-lat_migne1847 l.39405, 41824, 42849)

claims.claim: Isidore: 'duo ejusdem libri de Veritate praedestinationis, ad episcopos missi'
claims.witness: Isidore, De viris illustribus 27 (isidore-seville_sententiae-eccl-officiis-historia-gothorum-pl83-lat_migne1860 l.122097-122098)

claims.claim: Letter XVII 'seu liber S. Fulgentii et aliorum quindecim episcoporum Africanorum, Ad Petrum diaconum et alios qui ex Oriente in causa fidei Romam missi sunt, de Incarnatione et Gratia Domini nostri Jesu Christi', signed by Datianus, Fortunatus, Boethus ... Quodvultdeus, Fulgentius and others
claims.witness: Letter XVII heading and salutation (fulgentius-ruspe_opera-contra-arianos-pl65-lat_migne1847 l.29473-29487)

claims.claim: Fulgentius died before finishing his answer to Count Reginus's questions; 'Ferrandus absolvit ejus discipulus, ipso flagitante Regino'
claims.witness: Gallandi, Notitia on Ferrandus (facundus-ferrandus-caesarius-dionysius-pl67-lat_migne1865 l.68395-68404)

claims.claim: Isidore: 'Fulgentius [OCR Fulgentus], Afer, ecclesiae Ruspensis [OCR luspensis] episcopus, in confessione fidei clarus, in Scripturis divinis copiosissime eruditus, in loquendo quoque dulcis, in docendo ac disserendo subtilis, scripsit multa'; 'A Thrasamundo rege idem beatus Fulgentius disputavit'
claims.witness: Isidore, De viris illustribus 27 (isidore-seville_sententiae-eccl-officiis-historia-gothorum-pl83-lat_migne1860 l.122085-122088, 122190)

claims.claim: 'who was called the Augustin of the sixth century (died 533)'
claims.witness: Philip Schaff, A Sketch of the Life of St. Augustin (npnf101_augustine-confessions-letters l.1422)

claims.claim: Feast: 'Martyrol. romain, 1er janvier; Martyrol. hieronym., Kal. Jan.'; bishop 'FULGENTIUS Ruspensis, 508-533'
claims.witness: Joseph Mesnage (mesnage_afrique-chretienne-eveches-ruines-antiques-fra_1912 l.9817-9819, OCR 'Rusi^ensis', 'Marli/rol.')

claims.claim: He died 'die kalendarum Januariarum post peractam vesperam ... annum sui episcopatus agens vicesimum quintum, vitae autem totius sexagesimum quintum'; no year is given
claims.witness: The Life of Fulgentius, by a disciple, PL 65, ch. 29 §62 (fulgentius-ruspe_opera-contra-arianos-pl65-lat_migne1847 l.10028-10032)

claims.claim: The English Life: 'the first day of a new yeare, the 25. yeare of his episcopall dignity, the 60. of his lyfe' (OCR 'ofa', 'ycarcof', 'Iyfe')
claims.witness: Anonymous English abridged Life, 1605, made from Surius's text (margin 'Suarius [OCR] 1. die Ianuarij') (victor-of-vita_memorable-and-tragical-history-persecution-eng_1605 l.9327-9329)

claims.claim: Gallandi: 'Et Baronius quidem ait, summum illud Ecclesiae Africanae decus anno 529 supremum diem obiisse ipsis calendis Januarii. Pagius vero et Bollandus Baronium pene assectantur'
claims.witness: Gallandi, Notitia on Ferrandus (facundus-ferrandus-caesarius-dionysius-pl67-lat_migne1865 l.68416-68420)

claims.claim: Gallandi is a scholar who edited the early Christian writers: PL 67 prints its notices 'ex Gallandii Bibliotheca', from his Bibliotheca veterum patrum, and Otto names its editor in full, 'curavit ANDREAS GALLANDI', with the title 'Bibliotheca veterum Patrum antiquorumque Scri- ptorum ecclesiasticorum'. The brief's 'The scholar Andrea Gallandi' rests on this
claims.witness: PL 67 (facundus-ferrandus-caesarius-dionysius-pl67-lat_migne1865 l.379); Otto (tatian_oratio-ad-graecos-grc-lat_otto1851 l.20101-20103)

claims.claim: Baronius is a cardinal: 'Caesaris Baronii cardinalis' (OCR 'Csesaris')
claims.witness: PL 67 (facundus-ferrandus-caesarius-dionysius-pl67-lat_migne1865 l.11102)

claims.claim: Chifflet, quoted by Gallandi, put the death 'die sabbati, calendis Januarii, anno ... Dionysiano 555' and the Life's writing 'anno transacto post mortem Fulgentii, nempe anno Christi 554'; Noris, quoting Chifflet, has him say the Life was published 'anno 534' ('addens anno 534 opus illud evulgasse'). The 555 and 554 are misreadings of 533 and 534 (3 read as 5 in this print), since 534 is one year after the death; Noris 'Chiffletio adhaerens' gives 'anno 554 [=533?], non autem anno 334 [OCR, reading uncertain]'
claims.witness: Gallandi, Notitia on Ferrandus, quoting Chifflet and Noris (facundus-ferrandus-caesarius-dionysius-pl67-lat_migne1865 l.68411-68422, 68666-68668, 68684-68686); OCR digits uncertain throughout l.68410-68694

claims.claim: Migne heads Fulgentius's works 'ANNO DOMINI DXXXIII' (OCR 'DXXX1II'), 533
claims.witness: PL 65 (fulgentius-ruspe_opera-contra-arianos-pl65-lat_migne1847 l.6996)

claims.claim: 'Fulgentius natus est ann. 464 (Vita S. Fulg. cap. 1), Ruspensem Ecclesiam regendam suscepit ann. 504 (Cap. 17) ... fato functus est ann. 529 (Cap. 30)'

contested_claims.claim: Who wrote the Life of Fulgentius
contested_claims.sides: Ferrandus of Carthage: P. Chifflet (1649), as Migne's note reports (fulgentius-ruspe_opera-contra-arianos-pl65-lat_migne1847 l.7961-7963), with Pithou, Miraeus, Christianus Lupus and Natalis Alexander, and Gallandi himself ('ut censeo') (facundus-ferrandus-caesarius-dionysius-pl67-lat_migne1865 l.68661, 68670-68678). Not shown: the note in Migne's edition says others are not convinced, since the author seems never to have left Fulgentius's side (fulgentius-ruspe_opera-contra-arianos-pl65-lat_migne1847 l.7964-7967); Noris, Pagi, Mangeant and Fontanini, per Gallandi (facundus-ferrandus-caesarius-dionysius-pl67-lat_migne1865 l.68678-68682). The Life names itself only as by 'a certain disciple' (fulgentius-ruspe_opera-contra-arianos-pl65-lat_migne1847 l.7912). Kept consistent with the approved Ferrandus profile.

contested_claims.claim: The year of his death
contested_claims.sides: 529: Baronius, nearly followed by Pagi and Bolland, as Gallandi reports (facundus-ferrandus-caesarius-dionysius-pl67-lat_migne1865 l.68416-68420); Garnier's dissertation in PL 48 (marius-mercator_opera-omnia-lat_migne-pl48 l.22206). 533: Chifflet and Noris as Gallandi quotes them, with the figures misread as 555/554 (facundus-ferrandus-caesarius-dionysius-pl67-lat_migne1865 l.68411-68422, 68684-68686); Migne's heading (fulgentius-ruspe_opera-contra-arianos-pl65-lat_migne1847 l.6996); Mesnage (mesnage_afrique-chretienne-eveches-ruines-antiques-fra_1912 l.9817); Schaff (npnf101_augustine-confessions-letters l.1422). The Life gives no year (fulgentius-ruspe_opera-contra-arianos-pl65-lat_migne1847 l.10028-10032).

contested_claims.claim: How many bishops Thrasamund exiled to Sardinia
contested_claims.sides: 120: Victor of Tunnuna (chronica-minora-2_marcellinus-victor-tunnunensis-biclaro-isidore-mgh-aa-11-lat_mommsen1894 l.18321) and Isidore (isidore-seville_sententiae-eccl-officiis-historia-gothorum-pl83-lat_migne1860 l.120079). contested_claims.claim: The year of Thrasamund's death
contested_claims.sides: 523: Victor of Tunnuna in Mommsen's year (chronica-minora-2_marcellinus-victor-tunnunensis-biclaro-isidore-mgh-aa-11-lat_mommsen1894 l.18609-18611); Mesnage (mesnage_afrique-chretienne-eveches-ruines-antiques-fra_1912 l.1494). 525: the PL 65 prolegomena (fulgentius-ruspe_opera-contra-arianos-pl65-lat_migne1847 l.7447), possibly an OCR 5 for 3.

claims.claim: Identifiers: Ferrandus is 'noster diaconus Carthaginiensis' in Gallandi's notice; Severinus is 'Noricorum apostoli' (Gallandi) and 'St. Severinus of Noricum' (Foulke); Proba is 'virginem sacram'

claims.claim: 'When Count Pierius compelled all to depart, the venerable Lucillus, then our priest, was not unmindful of the command of Severinus. After he had ended singing with the monks the vesper psalms, he bade the place of burial to be opened. When it was uncovered, a fragrance of such sweetness surrounded us who stood by, that we fell on the earth for joy and wonder.' (the brief capitalizes the quote's first word 'a'). The brief's 'forced the Romans out of Noricum's Danube towns' keeps to Eugippius's own scope: Onoulf 'ordered all the Romans to migrate to Italy' (l.3927-3928, hyphen break 'or- dered'), and the provincials 'abandoned the towns on the banks of the Danube' (l.3976-3977). Robinson's note to that sentence: 'Julius Jung ... believes that the exodus was less general than the words of Eugippius would seem to imply ... it is obvious that there was no general withdrawal from Noricum Mediterraneum' (l.3979-3986)
claims.witness: Eugippius, Life of Severinus ch. XLIV, tr. Robinson (eugippius_life-of-saint-severinus_robinson1914 l.3957-3963)

claims.claim: The body was put in a casket, 'placed in a wagon drawn by horses, and presently carried forth. All the provincials made the journey in our company'; the monks bring it to Italy (Mount Feleter, l.4019-4022)
claims.witness: Life ch. XLIV, Robinson (eugippius_life-of-saint-severinus_robinson1914 l.3971-3976, 4019-4022); Robinson's table: 'The body of Severinus is disinterred, and is accompanied by the monks to Mount Feleter, in Italy' (l.4871-4873)

claims.claim: Barbaria invited 'our venerable priest Marcianus, and also the whole brotherhood'; 'with the authorization of Saint Gelasius, pontiff of the Roman see, and received by the people of Naples with reverent obsequies, the body was laid to rest by the hands of Saint Victor the bishop in the Lucullan castle, in a mausoleum which Barbaria had built'
claims.witness: Life ch. XLVI, Robinson (eugippius_life-of-saint-severinus_robinson1914 l.4035-4050)

claims.claim: 'A monastery, built at the same place to the memory of the blessed man, still endures.'
claims.witness: Life ch. XLVI, Robinson (eugippius_life-of-saint-severinus_robinson1914 l.4198-4199)

claims.claim: 'Marcianus the monk, who was afterward priest, and who preceded me in the headship of the monastery'
claims.witness: Life ch. XXXVII, Robinson (eugippius_life-of-saint-severinus_robinson1914 l.3380-3381)

claims.claim: 'S. Eugipius, abbas Lucullanensis oppidi, Neapoli Campaniae' (OCR 'Camp»ni»'); he wrote the Life for Paschasius; 'Scripsit et regulam monachis consistentibus in monasterio sancti Severini, quam eisdem moriens quasi testamentario jure reliquit'; 'Claruit post consulatum Importuni Junioris, Anastasio imperatore regnante' (OCR 'lmportuni')
claims.witness: Isidore of Seville, De viris illustribus c. 26, PL 83 (isidore-seville_sententiae-eccl-officiis-historia-gothorum-pl83-lat_migne1860 l.120436 list 'XXVI. Eugipius, ab'as Lucullanensis'; l.122075-122082; heading 'DE VIRIS ILLUSTRIBUS LIBER' l.120266)

claims.claim: Contemporaries address him as priest: Paschasius 'to the holy and ever most beloved priest Eugippius'; Dionysius Exiguus 'sacro Eugipio presbytero'; Ferrandus 'Domino beatissimo fratri Eugippio presbytero Ferrandus exiguus'; Fulgentius 'sancto fratri et compresbytero Eugyppio' (OCR 'sancio', 'compresbylero', 'Eucyppio'); the edition's heading of Fulgentius's letter reads 'AD EUGYPPIUM ABBATEM' (OCR 'EUGYPP1UM')
