claims.claim: Letter to Paschasius: 'About two years ago, in the consulship of Impor-tunus, a letter of a noble layman, directed to a priest, was offered me to read. It contained the life of Bassus a monk ... When I learned that some were making copies of this letter, I began to reflect, and also to declare to the clergy, that the great miracles which the divine power had wrought through Saint Severinus ought not to be hidden.' (hyphen break 'Impor- tunus')
claims.witness: Eugippius, Letter to Paschasius, Robinson (eugippius_life-of-saint-severinus_robinson1914 l.278-288)

claims.claim: 'In response to this offer, I prepared a memoir, filled full with testimonies from the daily narrations of the elder brethren, with which I was perfectly familiar.'
claims.witness: Letter to Paschasius (eugippius_life-of-saint-severinus_robinson1914 l.293-297)

claims.claim: He commits the materials to Paschasius: 'now I commit the materials to the architect, whose hands shall be thy eloquence'; 'Illustrious minister of Christ, thou hast the memoir. From it make by thy editorial care a profitable work.' The brief's 'sent it to Paschasius to polish' and the card's 'to work up' tell this
claims.witness: Letter to Paschasius and close of the Life (eugippius_life-of-saint-severinus_robinson1914 l.361-363, 4204-4205)

claims.claim: Robinson: 'A.D. 509' for Importunus's consulship; 'at the time of his writing (511)'; table: '511. Eugippius, second abbot of the monastery of Saint Severinus at the Lucullan castle, sends the Life of Severinus to Deacon Paschasius.' Robinson gives 511 without 'about'
claims.witness: G. W. Robinson, notes and Chronological Table (eugippius_life-of-saint-severinus_robinson1914 l.301, 2133-2134, 4908-4910)

claims.claim: Mommsen: 'Eugippii vitam Severini editam a. 511, quam citat c. 45' (the Anonymus Valesianus cites the Life); the excerpts are 'excerptis Eugippianis c. 45-48'
claims.witness: Theodor Mommsen, introduction to the Anonymus Valesianus (prosper_chronica-minora-1-lat_mommsen1892 l.33384, 33414); apparatus on c. 45-48 naming Severinus and 'odoachar' (l.40399-40407)

claims.claim: Foulke: 'An Italian monk, the pupil of St. Severinus of Noricum, who wrote about 511 a life of the saint'; 'Eugippius' biography of St. Severinus was used by Paul only once'
claims.witness: W. D. Foulke, notes to Paul the Deacon (paul-the-deacon_history-of-the-langobards_foulke1907 l.15630-15638)

claims.claim: First person at the deathbed: 'while we could hardly make the responses, he fell asleep in the Lord'; at the grave 'surrounded us who stood by'; 'Even in the lifetime of Saint Severinus, I never heard other particulars in regard to his native place than those I have related', having just related that his speech 'revealed a man of purest Latin stock' and that he went first 'into some desert place of the East' (l.446-448): he heard no more than that, not nothing
claims.witness: Life ch. XLIII-XLIV and Letter (eugippius_life-of-saint-severinus_robinson1914 l.3836-3837, 3962-3963, 446-448, 477-479)

claims.claim: He names informants: 'We heard the amazing story from Marcianus, a citizen of the same town, later our priest'; 'I learned what I have reported from the account of Marcus the subdeacon and Maternus the janitor'
claims.witness: Life (eugippius_life-of-saint-severinus_robinson1914 l.1829-1831, 2235-2237)

claims.claim: Gallandi: 'Italus fuit Eugippius, sancti Severini Noricorum apostoli et Gelasii papae discipulus, atque abbas Lucullanensis prope Neapolim Campaniae' (OCR 'zpostoli', 'pap:e', 'Lucu!lanensis', 'Campanis')
claims.witness: Andrea Gallandi, notice on Ferrandus, reprinted in PL 67 (facundus-ferrandus-caesarius-dionysius-pl67-lat_migne1865 l.68024-68026; '[Ex Gallandio.]' l.67839)

claims.witness: Lauchert (lauchert_kanones-altkirchlichen-concilien-lat-grc_1896 l.774); Peiper (avitus-vienne_opera-mgh-aa-6-2-lat_peiper1883 l.171)

claims.claim: Robinson: 'Eugippius, whose earlier years were spent in the Danubian lands, tells of conditions there as he remembers them'
claims.witness: Robinson's note (eugippius_life-of-saint-severinus_robinson1914 l.2129-2131)

claims.claim: Cassiodorus: 'Convenit etiam ut presbyteri Eugippii opera necessario legere debeatis, quem nos quoque vidimus, virum quidem non usque adeo saecularibus litteris eruditum, sed divinarum Scripturarum lectione plenissimum. Hic ad parentem nostram Probam virginem sacram ex operibus sancti Augustini valde altissimas quaestiones ac sententias, ac diversas res deflorans, in uno corpore ... et in trecentis triginta octo capitulis collocavit.' Sigebert, as Gallandi quotes him, calls the source 'libros Augustini episcopi Hipponensis' (PL 67 l.68093-68094, OCR 'fIip- pouensis'), hence 'Augustine of Hippo' in the brief and card. Clean wording from Gallandi's reprint (OCR 'mos', 'sv-eularibus', 'oruditum', 'tr ginta ccto ea-pitulis'); the PL 70 text is the same in broken two-column OCR, heading 'De abbate Eugipio et abbate Dionysio' (OCR 'abbatc liuyipio ei ubbWe Dionijaio')
claims.witness: Cassiodorus, Institutiones I.23 (cassiodorus_opera-institutiones-pl70-lat_migne1847 l.83524-83531); Gallandi's reprint (facundus-ferrandus-caesarius-dionysius-pl67-lat_migne1865 l.68027-68031, 68065-68072)

claims.claim: Gallandi on the Excerpta's preface: made 'cohortante Marino abbate', dedicated 'dominae merito venerabili et fructu sacrae virginitatis in Christi gratia semper illustri Probae', 'ut ipsemet in praefatione profitetur' (OCR 'dominx', 'saerz', "'rob:e"); Krusch quotes the opening 'Cohortante domno meo Marino abbate Eugippius excerpta ex opp. Augustini'
claims.witness: facundus-ferrandus-caesarius-dionysius-pl67-lat_migne1865 l.68073-68079; passiones-vitaeque-sanctorum-merovingici-mgh-srm-3-lat_krusch1896 l.13365

claims.claim: Dionysius Exiguus to Eugippius: 'Sancto venerationis tuae studio pro meis viribus obsecutus, beati Gregorii Nysseni episcopi librum De Conditione hominis e Graeca locutione converti' (OCR 'tu:', 'Nysseui', 'homisis', 'Gr»ca'); heading 'In versionem ab se factam libri Gregorii Nysseni, De Conditione seu opificio hominis'
claims.witness: Dionysius Exiguus, letter in PL 67 (facundus-ferrandus-caesarius-dionysius-pl67-lat_migne1865 l.27735-27747)

claims.claim: Ferrandus, Ep. IV 'Ad Eugippium presbyterum. De essentia Trinitatis, et de duabus Christi naturis'; 'consider quales habeat vires ab Ariano comite nuper proposita quaestio' (OCR 'LUGIPPJUM PRESDYTERUM', 'labeatvires', 'proposi:a')
claims.witness: Ferrandus of Carthage, Ep. IV, PL 67 (facundus-ferrandus-caesarius-dionysius-pl67-lat_migne1865 l.70146-70154)

claims.claim: Paschasius ('Paschasius, Roman deacon', Robinson's index, l.5838): 'Thou hast sent me a memoir to which the eloquence of the trained writer can add nothing, and in a short compendium hast produced a work which the whole church can read'; 'The deeds of the good cannot perish with time'; 'I have thought it best not to try to make any addition to thy work'
claims.witness: Paschasius, Letter to Eugippius, Robinson (eugippius_life-of-saint-severinus_robinson1914 l.4222-4225, 4231, 4254-4255)

claims.claim: Paschasius, answering the memoir: 'it is one thing to relate what we have been told, quite another thing, to draw from the stores of our own experience. The virtues of teachers are particularly visible in their daily life, and consequently are more easily depicted by their pupils.' The brief's 'Paschasius replies that teachers are more easily portrayed by their pupils' tells this; he replies to the memoir, explaining why he adds nothing; it is Paschasius's reading of Eugippius as Severinus's pupil, the one ancient witness on the question
claims.witness: Paschasius, Letter to Eugippius, tr. Robinson (eugippius_life-of-saint-severinus_robinson1914 l.4255-4260)

claims.claim: Robinson's preface quotes Teuffel: 'the incom-parable biography of Saint Severinus' (hyphen break 'incom- parable')
claims.witness: Robinson, Preface (eugippius_life-of-saint-severinus_robinson1914 l.117-118)

claims.claim: Severinus died 'on the eighth of January' with no year; the Life tells his deeds and miracles in Noricum; Paschasius: 'Saint Severinus, who dwelt in the provinces bordering on the Pannonias'. The brief's 'a holy man of the Danube borderlands' rests on this and on the Life's Danube towns ('They abandoned the towns on the banks of the Danube', l.3976-3977)
claims.witness: Life (eugippius_life-of-saint-severinus_robinson1914 l.3835, 3976-3977, 4226-4227)

claims.claim: Arevalo's note: 'Eugipium, quem Cassiodorus se vidisse ait, alium juniorem Eugipium esse, Fabricius cum aliis observat' (OCR 'Fabririus'); 'Importunus consul anno Christi 509' (OCR 'Mnportunus'); the edition is 'recensente Faustino Arevalo'
claims.witness: Arevalo's notes to Isidore, PL 83 (isidore-seville_sententiae-eccl-officiis-historia-gothorum-pl83-lat_migne1860 l.122109-122115; l.399)

claims.claim: Gallandi rejects 'commentum de duobus Eugippiis, quorum alter italus, Africanus alter fuerit' held by Miraeus, Bollandus and Cave, and blames Sigebert: 'Eugippius abbas hortatu Reudacis ... Fuit tempore Pelagii II et imperatoris Tiberii Constantini'; Gallandi: Sigebert 'bifariam errat'. Gallandi does not name Fabricius, so he answers a like view, not Arevalo's report; Sigebert is 'Sigeb. Gembl.' (l.67956), Sigebert of Gembloux
claims.witness: Gallandi, PL 67 (facundus-ferrandus-caesarius-dionysius-pl67-lat_migne1865 l.68085-68104)

claims.claim: The Lucullan castle: Robinson 'Now Pizzofalcone.'; Hodgkin's index 'Lucullanum, Castrum (Castel dell Ovo, at Naples)'; Kihn 'Priester und Abt des Klosters Lucullanum, zwischen Neapel und Puzzuoli'
claims.witness: eugippius_life-of-saint-severinus_robinson1914 l.4060; cassiodorus_variae-letters-hodgkin1886 l.24138; kihn_theodor-von-mopsuestia-junilius-africanus-instituta-lat-deu_1880 l.11632-11633

claims.claim: Kihn calls him 'einen Schüler des hl. Severin'
claims.witness: Heinrich Kihn (kihn_theodor-von-mopsuestia-junilius-africanus-instituta-lat-deu_1880 l.11642)

claims.claim: The Anonymus Valesianus is a Latin chronicle of Ostrogothic Italy: Mommsen's summary of its contents runs through Theodoric's reign (a. 519 Eutharicus consul ... a. 526)
claims.witness: prosper_chronica-minora-1-lat_mommsen1892 l.33490-33497

claims.claim: Cassiodorus as a statesman of Gothic Italy: Hodgkin, 'the statesman who, after spending thirty years at the Court of Theodoric and his daughter, spent thirty-three years more in the monastery which he had himself erected at Squillace'; and 'he became what we should call the Prime Minister of the Ostrogothic King Theodoric'. The brief's and card's 'Cassiodorus, a statesman of Gothic Italy' rests on these
claims.witness: Thomas Hodgkin, Introduction (cassiodorus_variae-letters-hodgkin1886 l.1090-1091, 1119-1121)

contested_claims.claim: Whether Eugippius was an eyewitness disciple of Severinus
contested_claims.sides: For: his first-person 'we' at the deathbed and the grave (eugippius_life-of-saint-severinus_robinson1914 l.3836, 3962) and 'Even in the lifetime of Saint Severinus' (l.477); Paschasius, who received the memoir, reads him as a pupil: teachers' virtues 'are more easily depicted by their pupils' (eugippius_life-of-saint-severinus_robinson1914 l.4255-4260); Gallandi 'Severini ... discipulus' (facundus-ferrandus-caesarius-dionysius-pl67-lat_migne1865 l.68025); Foulke 'the pupil of St. Severinus' (paul-the-deacon_history-of-the-langobards_foulke1907 l.15637); Kihn 'Schüler' (l.11642). Caution: Eugippius says the memoir rests on 'the daily narrations of the elder brethren' (l.295-296) and names informants (l.1829-1831, 2235-2237); no held line gives his age or office at Severinus's death.

contested_claims.claim: Whether the Eugippius Cassiodorus saw is the author of the Life
contested_claims.sides: Fabricius and others, reported in Arevalo's notes: a younger, different Eugippius (isidore-seville_sententiae-eccl-officiis-historia-gothorum-pl83-lat_migne1860 l.122113-122115). Gallandi: one man; the 'two Eugippii' (Italian and African) of Miraeus, Bollandus and Cave come from Sigebert's error (facundus-ferrandus-caesarius-dionysius-pl67-lat_migne1865 l.68085-68104).

contested_claims.claim: Where the Lucullan castle stood
contested_claims.sides: Robinson: now Pizzofalcone (l.4060). Hodgkin's index: Castel dell'Ovo, at Naples (l.24138). Kihn: between Naples and Pozzuoli (l.11633). Eugippius and Isidore: at Naples, without more.

claims.claim: Michael: Jacob of Edessa 'alla au monastère d'Aphtonia et y prit l'habit monastique. Il y étudia soigneusement les Psaumes en langue grecque' (OCR 'monas-^ tère', 'monas- tique'); he took the habit there and studied the Psalms there, which the brief tells as 'became a monk at the monastery of Aphthonia and studied the Psalms there in Greek'. That this is the writer's house is disputed (contested claim 'Whether Beith-Aphthonia is the Kenneshre house'); Bar Hebraeus: 'in monasterio Aphtonii seu Kenserinensi graecam linguam et sacrorum librorum lectionem accurate didicit' (in the monastery of Aphtonius, or of Kenneshre, he learned Greek and the reading of the holy books with care; OCR 'Jacobiis', 'graccani', 'lectio- nem'). The brief's close 'Bar Hebraeus calls it the Kenneshre monastery' rests on this; 'Kenneshre' is the card's English form of his 'Kenserinensi'. Michael likewise calls the monastery of Bar Aphtonia 'appelé de Qennésrîn' (l.29097-29098)

claims.claim: Brooks's note: 'The monastery which John son of Aphthonia established at Kenneshre on the Euphrates after it had been expelled from Seleueia [OCR Seleucia]'. The note is to 'Dimet from the monastery of Aphthonia in the eity [OCR] of Laodicea', made a metropolitan; the same list has 'Sergius from the monastery of Aphthonia in Charrhae'. In this list of consecrations each city is the see (Laodicea, Seleucia, Tarsus, Kenneshrin, Charrhae, Sura), so Charrhae is Sergius's see and the line names one monastery of Aphthonia, not two. contested_claims.claim: Whether the writer of the Life is the archimandrite John bar Aphthonia of Kenneshre
contested_claims.sides: Distinct: Kugener calls the attribution in Add. 14,731 false (zacharias-scholasticus_vie-de-severe-po2-syr-fra_kugener1903 l.13050-13052, 16826-16828); the Life reports bar Aphthonia's death in the third person (l.16605-16667); Assemani names two Johns as abbots of the house (B.O. I l.101085-101088). Same man: Chabot, who writes of 'la vie rédigée par Jean Bar Aphtonia', his 'probablement' being about the source of Michael's fragment (michael-the-syrian_chronique-tome2-livres-viii-xi-fra_chabot1901 l.14077-14079); R. Duval, 'la vie de ce patriarche écrite par Jean bar Aphtonia', his 'probablement' likewise about the extract (theopistus_histoire-de-dioscore-journal-asiatique-1903-fra_nau1903 l.33829-33830); Brooks, 'the later life by John archimandrite of Kenneshre' (Select Letters I l.191); the Library header (l.6-7). The approved Severus card names the writer 'John, head of the monastery of Beth Aphthonia' and does not equate him.

contested_claims.claim: The year of the archimandrite's death
contested_claims.sides: The extract Kugener prints: 4 November, in the entry for Severus's death in 849 of the Greeks, which Brooks gives as 538 (severus-of-antioch_select-letters-book6-part1_brooks1903 l.240-241) (zacharias-scholasticus_vie-de-severe-po2-syr-fra_kugener1903 l.19884-19886); Michael: 'en cette année' (michael-the-syrian_chronique-tome2-livres-viii-xi-fra_chabot1901 l.18414-18417); Elias of Nisibis: 850 of the same count, after Severus in 849 (elias-of-nisibis_opus-chronologicum-lat_brooks-chabot-csco1910 l.5366-5373); the Life: fifteen days after Severus's last letter, before Severus's death (zacharias-scholasticus_vie-de-severe-po2-syr-fra_kugener1903 l.16666).

contested_claims.claim: Whether Beith-Aphthonia is the Kenneshre house
contested_claims.sides: Michael's name 'monastère de Bar Aphtonia, appelé de Qennésrîn' (michael-the-syrian_chronique-tome2-livres-viii-xi-fra_chabot1901 l.29097-29098) and Brooks's note (john-ephesus_lives-eastern-saints-po19-mixed-issue_brooks1926 l.10661), and Bar Hebraeus's 'in monasterio Aphtonii seu Kenserinensi' for the house where Jacob of Edessa learned Greek (barhebraeus_chronicon-ecclesiasticum-vol1-lat_abbeloos-lamy1872 l.17306-17307), tie it to Kenneshre; against these, the heading of the Life gives no place for Beith-Aphthonia, and the tie rests on later names and Brooks's note. John of Ephesus's 'Sergius from the monastery of Aphthonia in Charrhae' (john-ephesus_lives-eastern-saints-po19-mixed-issue_brooks1926 l.10650-10651) gives Charrhae as Sergius's see, not a second monastery.

claims.witness: Stokes, introduction (stokes_lives-of-saints-from-the-book-of-lismore-iri-eng_1890 l.218-219, OCR 'Lisinorc')

claims.claim: Stokes's footnote to 'this city' in the Life ('Colombcille's household came from Hi to this city', l.22755-22756): 'That is, Clonmacnois, where this Life of Ciarán was composed.' This is Stokes's view; the card's 'that Whitley Stokes says was composed at Clonmacnois' gives it as his
claims.witness: Stokes, footnote 2 (stokes_lives-of-saints-from-the-book-of-lismore-iri-eng_1890 l.22789)

claims.claim: Written down long after him: Stokes says the scribes modernised older copies, leaving 'a mixed language, in which Old-Irish forms appear side by side with those belonging to the late Middle, and even Modern, periods'; the book itself is of the fifteenth century. How long after him the Life was first composed no source used here says
claims.witness: Stokes (stokes_lives-of-saints-from-the-book-of-lismore-iri-eng_1890 l.3250-3257, l.218-219)

claims.claim: The Life is hagiography, a saint's Life, as the brief says: it calls him 'sanctus Ciaranus sacerdos et apostolus Christi' and makes him 'A man full of likeness in many ways to Jesus Christ'
claims.witness: Lismore Life (stokes_lives-of-saints-from-the-book-of-lismore-iri-eng_1890 l.21961-21962, OCR 'Chrish\\'; l.22914)

claims.claim: Stokes: 'Making a living stag's antlers serve as a bookstand is a stock miracle in Celtic hagiology' (note to §4136 of the Life; OCR 'slock')
claims.witness: Stokes, notes (stokes_lives-of-saints-from-the-book-of-lismore-iri-eng_1890 l.28901-28903)

claims.claim: Tirechan: '[Iustus] diaconus Patricii ... in senectute sua bona babtitzauit Ciaranum filium artificis quando senex ac plenus dierum fuit. Interest hautem inter mortem Patricii et Cerani natiuitatem, ut peritissimi numerorum aestimant, cxl. annorum, et babtitzatus est Ceranus ex libro Patricii, a diacono Iusto in meo conspectu.' Round brackets in the file are Stokes's restorations of a damaged page: 'Cia)ranum', 'sen(ex)', '(et Cer)ani (na)tiuitatem (ut peri)tissimi', '(in meo)', 'd(iaco)n(us Patricii)'. The words 'filium artificis', 'babtitzatus est Ceranus ex libro Patricii, a diacono Iusto' and 'cxl. annorum' are read
claims.witness: Tirechan, Collections, ed. Stokes (stokes_tripartite-life-of-patrick-v2-lat-muirchu-tirechan-confession_1887 l.3466-3477, OCR 'scncctutc', 'acstimant', 'lusto')

claims.claim: The Lismore Life tells the same baptism as Tirechan: 'He was baptized by deacon Justus, for it was very meet that the righteous should be baptized by a righteous one'; and makes Justus his first tutor, 'his tutor, deacon Justus'. This is the one story of the Life that an earlier held source also tells (Tirechan, 'babtitzatus est Ceranus ex libro Patricii, a diacono Iusto', OCR 'lusto', stokes_tripartite-life-of-patrick-v2-lat-muirchu-tirechan-confession_1887 l.3476-3477)
claims.witness: Lismore Life (stokes_lives-of-saints-from-the-book-of-lismore-iri-eng_1890 l.22098-22100, l.22145)

claims.claim: Tirechan wrote in the late 600s: he complains that the 'familia Clono' holds Patrick's places by force 'post mortalitates nouissimas', and Stokes's note on these plagues reads 'A.D. 683, apparently'
claims.witness: Tirechan (stokes_tripartite-life-of-patrick-v2-lat-muirchu-tirechan-confession_1887 l.3186-3189); Stokes's note 11 (stokes_tripartite-life-of-patrick-v2-lat-muirchu-tirechan-confession_1887 l.3224, OCR 'G83')

claims.claim: Stokes's note on 'familia Clono': ''of Cluain (maccu Nois?).' — Stokes's identification, with his own query
claims.witness: Stokes, note 10 (stokes_tripartite-life-of-patrick-v2-lat-muirchu-tirechan-confession_1887 l.3222)

claims.claim: Tirechan wrote of Patrick: his Collections are documents concerning Patrick, headed 'Tirechan episcopus haec scripsit ex ore uel libro Ultani episcopi'
claims.witness: Stokes ed. (stokes_tripartite-life-of-patrick-v2-lat-muirchu-tirechan-confession_1887 l.2208-2213, l.2273)

claims.claim: Adomnan: Columba 'was pleased to go to visit the Brethren who were dwelling in the Clonoensian monastery of St. Ceran (Clonmacnoise). And when they heard of his arrival, all of them from the little fields about the monastery ... following with the greatest alacrity the Abbot Alither, set out with one accord, going outside the enclosure of the monastery to meet St. Columba'; 'binding together a canopy of poles they had it carried by four men'
claims.witness: Adomnan, Life of Columba I.3, tr. Huyshe (adomnan_life-of-saint-columba_huyshe1905 l.2731-2752)

claims.claim: Adomnan wrote in the late 600s: Huyshe, 'Adamnan's abbacy was from 679 to 704, and thus this work was written between those years'
claims.witness: Huyshe, note (adomnan_life-of-saint-columba_huyshe1905 l.10426-10427)

claims.claim: Huyshe: Alither, 'Fourth abbot of Clonmacnoise. Died 599.' (Huyshe's note, not Adomnan's)
claims.witness: Huyshe (adomnan_life-of-saint-columba_huyshe1905 l.2836-2837)

claims.claim: 'Now Beoit, son of Olchan, of the Lathairn, of Mag Molt of Ulaid, was the earthly father of this Ciarán'; 'My father was Beoit, the wright'; he is 'the holy Ciarán, son of the wright'; by earthly descent 'son of the wright who built chariots, and (practised) every art besides'. Tirechan calls him 'filium artificis' (the craftsman's son). The brief's 'a craftsman' and the card's 'or craftsman' rest on these
claims.witness: Lismore Life (stokes_lives-of-saints-from-the-book-of-lismore-iri-eng_1890 l.22038-22046, l.21962, l.21966-21967); Tirechan (stokes_tripartite-life-of-patrick-v2-lat-muirchu-tirechan-confession_1887 l.3471)

claims.claim: 'So he asked his mother and his father for a cow, that he might take her with him when he went to learn. Ciarán's mother said she would not give him (the cow). So he blessed a cow of the kine, — Odar Ciaráin ("Ciarán's Dun") was her name thenceforward, — and she went thence with her calf after Ciarán to Clonard'
claims.witness: Lismore Life (stokes_lives-of-saints-from-the-book-of-lismore-iri-eng_1890 l.22226-22231)

claims.claim: 'Now the milk of that cow was parted among those twelve bishops with their households and with their guests, and it used to be enough for them all'; 'Now the Dun's hide is in Clonmacnois'
claims.witness: Lismore Life (stokes_lives-of-saints-from-the-book-of-lismore-iri-eng_1890 l.22248-22249, l.22257, OCR 'Hfe')

claims.claim: The Life sends him on: 'Thereafter Ciarán went to Aran to commune with Enna'; then to Inis Cathaig 'to bid farewell to Senán'; to Isel, where he 'dwelt along with the brethren'; to Inis Angin, where a priest 'gave the island up to him', Ciarán tells the brethren that a youth 'will be your abbot after me', and Enna Mac-Hui-Laigsi 'became abbot after Ciarán'; 'Three years, then, and three months dwelt Ciarán in Inis Angin'; then to Ard Tiprat, 'Here then we will stay'. The Life makes no one after Findian his teacher. The brief's 'The Life then takes him to Enda of Aran. Before Clonmacnois he led a house on the island of Inis Angin for three years' rests on this
claims.witness: Lismore Life (stokes_lives-of-saints-from-the-book-of-lismore-iri-eng_1890 l.22541, l.22563-22564, l.22592-22594, l.22640-22650, l.22667-22674)

claims.claim: 'Ard Tiprat ("the Height of the Well,") was its name at that time'
claims.witness: Lismore Life (stokes_lives-of-saints-from-the-book-of-lismore-iri-eng_1890 l.22672)

claims.claim: 'Howbeit Ciarán remained in that place for the space of seven months only when he went to heaven'; 'in the thirty-third year of his age, on the fifth of the ides of September'; 'when he looked at the sky, and the lofty air above his head, he said, "Awful is this way above."'
claims.witness: Lismore Life (stokes_lives-of-saints-from-the-book-of-lismore-iri-eng_1890 l.22804-22805, l.22815-22820)

claims.claim: The Life draws the parallel: 'Thirty and three years in the age of this man, as there are thirty and three years in the age of Christ.' No other source used here gives his age
claims.witness: Lismore Life (stokes_lives-of-saints-from-the-book-of-lismore-iri-eng_1890 l.22920-22921)

claims.claim: Annales Cambriae: 'c. Annus. Dormitatio Ciarani.' The margin year, printed by the OCR as '5i4', is the editor's; by his sequence (537 at xciii, 547 at ciii) it reads 544. The annal itself counts years only
claims.witness: Annales Cambriae, ed. John Williams ab Ithel (annales-cambriae-rolls-series-20-lat_williams-ab-ithel1860 l.2401-2408); same entry reprinted by Stokes (stokes_tripartite-life-of-patrick-v2-lat-muirchu-tirechan-confession_1887 l.13659)

claims.claim: Williams ab Ithel's preface lists 'the death of Ciaran, abbot of Cluan' among the annal's Irish entries
claims.witness: Williams ab Ithel, preface (annales-cambriae-rolls-series-20-lat_williams-ab-ithel1860 l.889-890)

claims.claim: O'Donovan: 'Kieran, Cianan.— This celebrated Irish saint died in the year 549. Cluain mac nois, or, as it is now anglicised, Clonmacnoise, was a famous monastery near the Shannon'
claims.witness: O'Donovan, note to the Annals of the Four Masters vol. III (four-masters_annals-of-the-kingdom-of-ireland-v3-1172-1378-gle-eng_odonovan1856 l.340-344)

claims.claim: The Bollandists, commenting on the Life of Enda: the vision of his monastery's future 'circa extremum Thuatalii Regis annum, Christi DXLIV' (OCR 'pxiiv'); 'S. Kieranus Cluanensis'
claims.witness: Acta Sanctorum, March III, commentary on Enda (acta-sanctorum_martii-tomus-3-lat-grc_palme1865 l.75805-75812)

claims.claim: Gilla Coemain's chronological poem, Stokes's English: 'TuathalMaelgarb's death with horror a year before Ciaran's obit'. A note in Stokes's edition, following O'Conor, probably dates the verses to 1072: 'The meaning probably is (as O'Conor says) that the new moon fell in 1071 on the 25th Dec., and that therefore there were seven days thence to Jan. 1, 1072, the year in which these verses were made' (OCR 'moaning', '(yConor')
claims.witness: Gilla Coemain's poem, ed. and tr. Stokes (stokes_tripartite-life-of-patrick-v2-lat-muirchu-tirechan-confession_1887 l.16366-16368; note l.15790-15797; page heads 'GILLA COEMAIN'S CHRONOLOGICAL POEM' l.15903, l.16314, OCR)

claims.claim: 'He is a different man from Ciaran of Saigir, and the Book of Lismore keeps the two apart': the Life tells how 'Ciarán, the Wright's son' went to 'Ciaran of Saigir', and 'Then the two Ciaráns made their union'
claims.witness: Lismore Life (stokes_lives-of-saints-from-the-book-of-lismore-iri-eng_1890 l.22768-22787)

claims.claim: Stokes's note: 'Ciarán of Saigir. Of this saint there is a Latin Life in the Codex Salmanticensis ... See also the Martyrology of Donegal, at March 5.' The Bollandists likewise distinguish 'Kierani Sagiriensis, non Cluanensis' (OCR 'Clua- nenjti')
claims.witness: Stokes, notes (stokes_lives-of-saints-from-the-book-of-lismore-iri-eng_1890 l.29003-29006); Acta Sanctorum, March I (acta-sanctorum_martii-tomus-1-lat_1735 l.70107-70108)

claims.claim: Stokes's index separates 'Ciaran mac intsair' (with 'Ceranus filius artificis') from 'of Saigir', 'of Belaih Duin' and 'Ciaran, son of Darerca, eps.'; the Lismore Life gives Ciaran of Clonmacnois a mother Darerca
claims.witness: Stokes, index (stokes_tripartite-life-of-patrick-v2-lat-muirchu-tirechan-confession_1887 l.22145-22152, OCR 'films', 'sou'); Lismore Life (stokes_lives-of-saints-from-the-book-of-lismore-iri-eng_1890 l.22038-22039)

claims.claim: In the Lismore Life of Colum Cille: 'Then he went to Clonmacnois with the hymn he had made for Ciarán.'
claims.witness: Lismore Life of Colum Cille (stokes_lives-of-saints-from-the-book-of-lismore-iri-eng_1890 l.17756)

claims.claim: The Lismore Life of Ciarán: 'A lamp, then, was he, blazing with the light of wisdom and instruction, as Colombcille said, — Lucerna hujus insulae'; Stokes's note: 'These words form part of a hymn quoted by Colgan ... beginning thus: Quantum Christe O Apostolum ... Lucerna huius insulae'
claims.witness: Lismore Life (stokes_lives-of-saints-from-the-book-of-lismore-iri-eng_1890 l.21979-21981, OCR 'insulce'); Stokes, note to §3957 (stokes_lives-of-saints-from-the-book-of-lismore-iri-eng_1890 l.28770-28776, OCR 'Lticerna')

claims.claim: 'Let the elders of this monastery keep the rules and the teachings and the customs which have been received from the master Ciarán : so that these are the rules and the customs which have been scattered abroad and brought to all the monasteries of the saints of Ireland'
claims.witness: Lismore Life (stokes_lives-of-saints-from-the-book-of-lismore-iri-eng_1890 l.21987-21991)

claims.claim: O'Donovan's Four Masters: 'Tiernagh O'Malone, successor of Kieran of Clonmacnoise, died'
claims.witness: Annals of the Four Masters, tr. O'Donovan (four-masters_annals-of-the-kingdom-of-ireland-v3-1172-1378-gle-eng_odonovan1856 l.393)

claims.claim: 'Now the saints of Ireland envied Ciarán for his goodness, and they betook themselves to the King of Heaven that his life might be shortened'
claims.witness: Lismore Life (stokes_lives-of-saints-from-the-book-of-lismore-iri-eng_1890 l.22841, l.22859, across a page of footnotes)

claims.claim: 'The cutting-off Ciarán's life, and putting Colomb-cille over sea, and expelling Mochuta from Raithin, those are the three wrong stories of Ireland's saints' (OCR 'cntting', 'Ciariin's')
claims.witness: Irish text 'Patrick and his leper', ed. and tr. Stokes (stokes_tripartite-life-of-patrick-v2-lat-muirchu-tirechan-confession_1887 l.17980-17982)

claims.claim: Roman Martyrology, 9 September, Bute's English: 'In Ireland, [in the sixth century,] the holy Abbat Ciaran, [founder of Clonmacnois.]' The brackets are Bute's additions. The offices peculiar to Ireland: 'September 9. St Ciaran ... Greater Double'
claims.witness: The Roman Breviary, autumn volume, tr. Bute (roman-breviary_bute1908 l.63615 heading 'Upon the 9th day of September', l.63676-63678; l.108727, l.108753-108757)

claims.claim: The feast in the Life: 'on the fifth of the ides of September' (= 9 September by the Roman reckoning, which the Breviary entry matches)
claims.witness: Lismore Life (stokes_lives-of-saints-from-the-book-of-lismore-iri-eng_1890 l.21969-21970, l.22816)

claims.claim: The Life of Enda in the Bollandists: 'S. Kieranus filius Fabri perveniens, septem annis in monasterii ... territorio fideliter serviens mansit ... trituratoris officium'; the Bollandists say the codex-writer Augustinus Magraidin 'ex duabus vetustioribus tam exiguo judicio consarcinavit'
claims.witness: Acta Sanctorum, March III (acta-sanctorum_martii-tomus-3-lat-grc_palme1865 l.76780-76784, l.75742-75747, OCR '4ngustinus')

claims.claim: Hugh Williams: 'Kieran (Cieran) the founder of Clonmacnois, were brought up at Clonard'
claims.witness: Williams, introduction to Gildas (gildas_de-excidio-britanniae-lorica-penitential-lat-eng_williams1899 l.9111-9112)

claims.claim: Name forms: 'Ciarán, son of the wright' (Lismore l.21962); 'Ciaran mac intsair' (Stokes's index, T l.22145); 'Ceranus' (Tirechan, T l.3476); 'Kieran' (O'Donovan, FM l.340); 'S. Kieranus Cluanensis' (Bollandists, AS3 l.75805)
claims.witness: stokes_lives-of-saints-from-the-book-of-lismore-iri-eng_1890; stokes_tripartite-life-of-patrick-v2-lat-muirchu-tirechan-confession_1887; four-masters_annals-of-the-kingdom-of-ireland-v3-1172-1378-gle-eng_odonovan1856; acta-sanctorum_martii-tomus-3-lat-grc_palme1865

claims.claim: Clonmacnois is near the Shannon: O'Donovan, 'a famous monastery near the Shannon'; the Life has him come to Ard Manntain 'beside the Shannon' before settling at Ard Tiprat
claims.witness: four-masters_annals-of-the-kingdom-of-ireland-v3-1172-1378-gle-eng_odonovan1856 l.343-344; stokes_lives-of-saints-from-the-book-of-lismore-iri-eng_1890 l.22669

claims.claim: He studied at Clonard under Findian, in the Life ('to go as a scholar to Findian of Clonard in order to learn wisdom'); leaving, he was 'bidding farewell to his tutor'
claims.witness: stokes_lives-of-saints-from-the-book-of-lismore-iri-eng_1890 l.22226-22227, l.22512

claims.claim: Role: founder (the Life's account of the first stake and founding at Cluain, l.22676-22701) and abbot (Williams ab Ithel, 'Ciaran, abbot of Cluan'; Bute's 'the holy Abbat Ciaran')
claims.witness: stokes_lives-of-saints-from-the-book-of-lismore-iri-eng_1890; annales-cambriae-rolls-series-20-lat_williams-ab-ithel1860 l.890; roman-breviary_bute1908 l.63677

claims.claim: Sixth century: the annal entries above (544 by the editor's margin; 549 by O'Donovan) and Bute's bracketed '[in the sixth century,]'
claims.witness: annales-cambriae-rolls-series-20-lat_williams-ab-ithel1860 l.2406; four-masters_annals-of-the-kingdom-of-ireland-v3-1172-1378-gle-eng_odonovan1856 l.340-341; roman-breviary_bute1908 l.63676

claims.claim: Tradition placing: 'Insular / Irish Monastic Christianity' (census, 450-664, Ireland, Iona, Northumbria), as used for Brigid of Kildare (era3 batch2)
claims.witness: cic-website/data/world-census.json movements

contested_claims.claim: The year of Ciaran's death
sides: Annales Cambriae, hundredth year, which John Williams ab Ithel's margin numbers 544 (annales-cambriae-rolls-series-20-lat_williams-ab-ithel1860 l.2406)
John O'Donovan: 549 (four-masters ... v3 l.340-341)
The Bollandists set the vision of his monastery at the end of Tuathal's reign, 544 (acta-sanctorum_martii-tomus-3 l.75810-75812)

contested_claims.claim: How long before Ciaran's death King Tuathal Maelgarb died
sides: Lismore Life: the night of the first stake, seven months before (stokes_lives ... l.22703-22705, 22804-22805)
Gilla Coemain's poem, Stokes's English: 'a year before Ciaran's obit' (stokes_tripartite ... l.16366-16368)

contested_claims.claim: His teachers and years before Clonmacnois
sides: Lismore Life: Findian his tutor (stokes_lives-of-saints-from-the-book-of-lismore-iri-eng_1890 l.22226-22227, 22512); Enna and Senán visited (l.22541, 22563-22564); Isel (l.22592-22594); abbot on Inis Angin three years and three months (l.22640-22669)
Bollandists' Life of Enda: Enda his master ('suo magistro', 'sui Abbatis Endei', acta-sanctorum_martii-tomus-3-lat-grc_palme1865 l.76789, 76803)

Bollandists' Life of Enda: seven years threshing for Enda on Aran (AS3 l.76780-76784); the Bollandists suggest he may have been Enda's novice before going to Senan (l.75805-75808, 'S. Kieranus Cluanensis, priusquam in S. Sennani disciplinam concederet, sub hoc S. Endeo monastica vitae potuisset tyrocinia')
Hugh Williams: brought up at Clonard (gildas ... l.9111-9112)

absent_details.detail: The year of his birth
absent_details.note: Searched every held file that names him (Ciaran/Ciarán/Kieran/Kiaran/Ceranus/Kieranus/Queran, Clonmac*/Cluain mac/Cluana-mic/Clono, mac intsair, filius artificis/fabri; case-insensitive grep across cic/texts .txt and .xml, then each hit within 100 characters of born/birth/nativ*/nascitur with a year). Tirechan gives only a reckoning of 140 years after Patrick's death, partly restored (T l.3474-3476); the Lismore Life gives a day and place (l.22080-22097). No year found.

absent_details.detail: The year Clonmacnois was founded
absent_details.note: Same search with founded/foundation/fundavit. The Lismore Life gives the day ('the eighth of the calends of February', l.22676), no year. The Bollandists' 544 dates Enda's vision of the monastery's future, not the founding (AS3 l.75810-75812). Bute's Martyrology gives the sixth century only.

absent_details.detail: Any writing of his
absent_details.note: No work under his name in any held file. Stokes mentions a poem attributed to him in the Book of Leinster, not held (L l.29014-29015). Verses the Life puts in his mouth are the Life's.

absent_details.detail: Any sixth-century witness
absent_details.note: The earliest held witnesses are Tirechan (after the plagues Stokes dates to 683) and Adomnan (written 679-704, Huyshe). The Annales Cambriae entry is in a later compilation.

claims.claim: The Constitutum is dated 'prid. Iduum Maiarum imperante domno nostro Iustiniano perpetuo Augusto anno XXVII ... in Constantinopolitana ciuitate'; Günther: 'Dat. die 14 Mai a. 553'
claims.witness: Collectio Avellana 83 (collectio-avellana_epistulae-imperatorum-pontificum-v1-lat_guenther1895 l.24223-24225); Otto Günther's note (collectio-avellana_epistulae-imperatorum-pontificum-v1-lat_guenther1895 l.18303)

claims.claim: The Constitutum was signed with sixteen bishops, Primasius among them; the council opened on 5 May 553 and Vigilius sent his ruling on 14 May
claims.witness: Heinrich Kihn: 'am 5. Mai 553 ... vom Kaiser eröffneten' and 'Bereits am 14. Mai hatte der Papst dem Kaiser ein Schriftstück über die drei Kapitel überreichen lassen, welches von sechzehn Bischöfen ... zwei Afrikanern, unterschrieben war. Zu letzteren zählt Primasius' (kihn_theodor-von-mopsuestia-junilius-africanus-instituta-lat-deu_1880 l.12603-12604, 12652-12657); cross-reference: council profile, Second Council of Constantinople (Council-Profiles/era3/second-council-of-constantinople-553.*)

claims.claim: The Three Chapters: writings tied to Theodore of Mopsuestia, Theodoret and Ibas that Justinian wanted condemned
claims.witness: Heinrich Kihn: the council condemned propositions 'aus den Schriften des Theodor von Mopsuestia', 'die Streitschriften des Theodoret gegen Cyrill und ... den Brief des Ibas an den Perser Maris' (kihn_theodor-von-mopsuestia-junilius-africanus-instituta-lat-deu_1880 l.12648-12652); cross-reference: council profile, Second Council of Constantinople, issue (Council-Profiles/era3/second-council-of-constantinople-553.entry.json)

claims.claim: Victor: 'Reparatus archiepiscopus Carthaginensis ecclesiae, Firmus Numidarum episcoporum primas et Primasius ac Verecundus concilii Byzaceni episcopi pro fidei causa ad urbem regiam eiusdem praecepto principis evocantur', under 'post consulatum Basili v. c. anno XI', which Mommsen's margin gives as 551 (OCR 'lieparatus', 'Pirmus', 'prinias')
claims.witness: Victor of Tunnuna, Chronicle (chronica-minora-2_marcellinus-victor-tunnunensis-biclaro-isidore-mgh-aa-11-lat_mommsen1894 l.19057-19062); the year 551 is Mommsen's; one manuscript, P(S), reads 'trium capitulorum pro causa', an interpolation by the apparatus (l.19098)

claims.claim: He came to Constantinople on the Three Chapters business: Kihn, 'Dass hierunter der Dreikapitelstreit zu verstehen ist, bedarf kaum der Bemerkung', of the bishops sent 'zur Besorgung der Angelegenheiten ihrer Kirchen'; the notice from Cave: 'ad res Ecclesiae Africanae procurandas Constantinopolim ... missi'
claims.witness: Heinrich Kihn (kihn_theodor-von-mopsuestia-junilius-africanus-instituta-lat-deu_1880 l.12548-12553); Notitia ex Cave, PL 68 (liberatus-victor-tunnunensis-primasius-junillus-pl68-lat_migne1866 l.34937-34941, 'ex Cave' l.34992)

claims.claim: Victor: 'Primasius quoque Acoemetensi monasterio relegatur, sed Boethio primate Byzaceni concilii morte praevento, ut ei succederet, memoratae damnationi protinus assensit reversusque ad sua, quae prius defendebat, validissimis persecutionibus impugnavit fidelibusque calumnias generando eorumque substantias auferendo. sed in quibus peccavit, laetari non potuit, siquidem postquam a catholicis sui concilii antistibus pro suis est praevaricationibus condemnatus, infelici morte extinguitur'. 'memoratae damnationi protinus assensit' (he at once agreed to the condemnation named above, that of the Three Chapters) is the brief's 'agreed to condemn the Three Chapters so that he might take his place'
claims.witness: Victor of Tunnuna, Chronicle, under 'anno XII' after Basilius, Mommsen's 552 (chronica-minora-2_marcellinus-victor-tunnunensis-biclaro-isidore-mgh-aa-11-lat_mommsen1894 l.19066, 19115-19121; OCR 'Byzaeeni', 'tidelibusque'); a hostile witness, writing for the Three Chapters; no second witness

claims.claim: Victor defended the Three Chapters: his chronicle records the African bishops' break with Vigilius 'pro defensione memoratorum trium capitulorum' and praises Facundus's books; Kihn: 'da Victor selbst als eifriger Vertheidiger der drei Kapitel schrieb'
claims.witness: Victor (chronica-minora-2_marcellinus-victor-tunnunensis-biclaro-isidore-mgh-aa-11-lat_mommsen1894 l.19047-19055); Kihn (kihn_theodor-von-mopsuestia-junilius-africanus-instituta-lat-deu_1880 l.12700-12701)

claims.claim: 'Wie viel Wahres an diesem Berichte ist, lässt sich schwer entscheiden; jedenfalls ist derselbe nicht frei von Parteifärbung, da Victor selbst als eifriger Vertheidiger der drei Kapitel schrieb'
claims.witness: Heinrich Kihn, Theodor von Mopsuestia und Junilius Africanus, 1880 (kihn_theodor-von-mopsuestia-junilius-africanus-instituta-lat-deu_1880 l.12698-12701)

claims.claim: Apparatus: 'aquimetensis libri'; 'laetari] ... coniectura puto, latere UP(E)'; 'fraudulenter] ... coniectura'; several clauses 'oblitterata in P(S)'
claims.witness: Mommsen's apparatus to Victor (chronica-minora-2_marcellinus-victor-tunnunensis-biclaro-isidore-mgh-aa-11-lat_mommsen1894 l.19164-19166)

claims.claim: Kihn quotes Victor as 'Primasius quoque Adrumetinus (Migne: Aquimetensis) monasterio relegatus', where Adrumetinus goes with Primasius ('Primasius of Hadrumetum too was sent to a monastery'), and in his own telling says only 'wurde er in ein Kloster relegiert', naming no monastery; he places the relegation after the May 553 refusal: 'Hierher fällt nach meinem Erachten die Relegation in ein Kloster, welche Victor von Tununum ad ann. 552 berichtet'
claims.witness: Kihn (kihn_theodor-von-mopsuestia-junilius-africanus-instituta-lat-deu_1880 l.12673-12675, 12690)

claims.claim: Migne's text of Victor: 'Primasius [OCR Piimasius] quoque Aquimetensis monasterio relegatus. Sed Boetio primate Byzanceni morte praevento'
claims.witness: Victor, PL 68 (liberatus-victor-tunnunensis-primasius-junillus-pl68-lat_migne1866 l.74709-74711)

claims.claim: Kihn reports, from Mansi IX 199, that on 8 May 553 in the second session the Western bishops still absent were invited, 'unter ihnen an erster Stelle Primasius'; 'Non sunt in nostro concilio praesentes de Africanis quidem Primasius, reverendissimus unus Byzacenae provinciae episcopus'; he answered 'Papa non praesente non venio'; the council resolved 'De Primasio quidem secundum ecclesiasticam traditionem opportune tempore quae oportet disponantur'
claims.witness: Heinrich Kihn (kihn_theodor-von-mopsuestia-junilius-africanus-instituta-lat-deu_1880 l.12620-12647), citing Mansi IX, which is not held; npnf214 has no 'Primas' hit

claims.claim: 'Anno 553, saepius licet advocatus, synodo oecumenicae interesse noluit; sed una cum aliis subscripsit Vigilii constituto pro tribus capitulis'
claims.witness: Notitia ex Cave, PL 68 (liberatus-victor-tunnunensis-primasius-junillus-pl68-lat_migne1866 l.34951-34957; OCR 'scepius', 'advocalus', 'cecumenicae')

claims.claim: Kihn: at the meeting of 14 August 551 where Vigilius condemned Theodore Askidas, the thirteen signers included 'Primasius von Adrumet und Verecundus von Junca'; Kihn first meets him at a Byzacene synod 'im Jahre 541', known from two rescripts of Justinian
claims.witness: Kihn (kihn_theodor-von-mopsuestia-junilius-africanus-instituta-lat-deu_1880 l.12554-12569; l.12515-12520), citing Mansi IX 60 and 111 and Baronius, not held

claims.claim: A note to Liberatus in Migne: 'Muneribus ditabantur.] De suis Africanis loquitur, Reparato Carthaginensi, Firmo Numidici, Primasio Byzaceni concilii primate, Verecundo'; Liberatus's own text names no one
claims.witness: Note to Liberatus, PL 68 (liberatus-victor-tunnunensis-primasius-junillus-pl68-lat_migne1866 l.82524-82527); derives from Victor

claims.claim: Gagny's dedication: 'Primasii Uticensis [OCR Ulitensis] in Africa episcopi commentarios', found at Saint-Theudère near Vienne 'annos supra mille' hidden; addressed to Francis I by 'Joannes Gagneius Parisinus theologus'
claims.witness: Dedication to Francis I, PL 68 (liberatus-victor-tunnunensis-primasius-junillus-pl68-lat_migne1866 l.35063-35065, 35122-35125)

claims.claim: 'Dass er Bischof von Utica gewesen, ist eine schon von Baronius ... zurückgewiesene Vermuthung des Trithemius'
claims.witness: Kihn (kihn_theodor-von-mopsuestia-junilius-africanus-instituta-lat-deu_1880 l.12523-12525)

claims.claim: Primosus, Reparatus's deacon and apocrisiarius, made bishop of Carthage while Reparatus lived; Mommsen reads 'Primosus', Migne 'Primasius diaconus'; Kihn: 'Eine ganz andere Persönlichkeit ist der oft mit dem Bischof von Adrumet verwechselte Erzbischof Primasius von Karthago'
claims.witness: Victor (chronica-minora-2_marcellinus-victor-tunnunensis-biclaro-isidore-mgh-aa-11-lat_mommsen1894 l.19068-19072); PL 68 (liberatus-victor-tunnunensis-primasius-junillus-pl68-lat_migne1866 l.74696-74701); Kihn (kihn_theodor-von-mopsuestia-junilius-africanus-instituta-lat-deu_1880 l.12680-12682)

claims.claim: Gallandi: 'Quid si Patrem appellavit Primasium ob venerandam canitiem, ipsemet aetate pariter ac sedis ... junior?' — a question, not evidence
claims.witness: Gallandi, Notitia on Junillus, PL 68 (liberatus-victor-tunnunensis-primasius-junillus-pl68-lat_migne1866 l.821-824; heading 'NOTITIA (ex Gallandio)' l.779)

claims.claim: Commentary: heading 'Commentariorum super Apocalypsim B. Joannis libri quinque'; prologue to 'vir illustris et religiose Castori'; 'si qua tamen a sancto quoque Augustino testimonia ... reperi, indubitanter adjunxi, sed etiam a Ticonio Donatista quondam certa, quae sano congruunt sensui, defloravi, et ... exundantia reprimens, importuna resecans, et impolita componens, catholico moderamine temperavi'. The Augustine is the bishop of Hippo, whose unfinished book on heresies Isidore names in his notice of Primasius; hence 'Augustine of Hippo' in the brief and card
claims.witness: Primasius, prologue to the Apocalypse commentary (liberatus-victor-tunnunensis-primasius-junillus-pl68-lat_migne1866 l.62636-62657; OCR 'QUIIVQUE', 'Casiori', 'Ticonio', 'olholico moderandne')

claims.claim: 'Multa quippe in ipso ejus opere reperi et supervacua, et inepta et sanae doctrinae contraria'
claims.witness: Prologue (liberatus-victor-tunnunensis-primasius-junillus-pl68-lat_migne1866 l.62657-62659)

claims.claim: 'Sicut autem pretiosa in stercore gemma a prudente debet curari, colligi, et repetitae dignitati ingenuae revocari, ita undecunque veritas clareat, catholicae defendenda est unitati. Huic enim soli competit quidquid veritas foris etiam personarit ... cum verae matri fuerit redditum' (wherever truth shines, it is to be defended for the Catholic unity; to it alone belongs whatever truth has sounded even outside ... when it has been given back to the true mother). The brief's 'wherever truth shines, it should be won back for the Catholic Church' rests on this
claims.witness: Prologue (liberatus-victor-tunnunensis-primasius-junillus-pl68-lat_migne1866 l.62678-62685; OCR 'aiitem', 'prudentc', 'repela', 'calliolicx def< ndenda', 'Huic cnim', 'compctit quitlqiiid verilas foris ctiam pcrsonarit', 'rcdditum')

claims.claim: Tyconius was a Donatist: Primasius's own 'Ticonio Donatista'; Burkitt's edition of his Book of Rules
claims.witness: Prologue (liberatus-victor-tunnunensis-primasius-junillus-pl68-lat_migne1866 l.62653); Burkitt (tyconius_liber-regularum_burkitt1894)

claims.claim: Cassiodorus: 'Nostris quoque temporibus Apocalypsis praedicta beati episcopi Primasii antistitis Africani studio minute ac diligenter quinque libris exposita est: quibus etiam liber unus, Quid faciat haereticum, cautissima disputatione subjunctus est'
claims.witness: Cassiodorus, Institutiones I.9 (cassiodorus_opera-institutiones-pl70-lat_migne1847 l.82379-82383; OCR 'Priraasii', 'niinuie', 'bbris'); in the chapter on the Apocalypse, after Augustine's City of God (l.82376-82378). 'Nostris quoque temporibus' (in our own times too; OCR 'Noslris quoque teitiporibus') is the brief's and card's 'a writer of his own time'

claims.claim: Cassiodorus: 'sanctus Primasius Justinianopoleos disertus antistes, sub titulo Quid haereticum facit, librum unum conscripsisse dignoscitur'
claims.witness: Cassiodorus, Expositio Psalmorum, Ps 118 (cassiodorus_opera-institutiones-pl70-lat_migne1847 l.60691-60693; OCR 'diserius')

claims.claim: Isidore: 'Primasius, Africanus episcopus, composuit sermone scholastico de Haeresibus tres libros directos ad Fortunatum episcopum, explicans in eis quod olim beatissimus Augustinus in libro Haereseon imperfectum, morte interveniente, reliquerat'
claims.witness: Isidore, De viris illustribus 22 (isidore-seville_sententiae-eccl-officiis-historia-gothorum-pl83-lat_migne1860 l.121854-121858)

claims.claim: The notice from Cave that Migne prints says the work on heresies is lost: 'Interiit jam dudum opus istud'. It then reports that the three books extant under the name Praedestinatus are, by an old manuscript Mabillon saw at Reichenau, given to Primasius: 'Opus sancti Primasii, discipuli Augustini, de Haeresibus numero XC', and doubts that note: 'quisquis hanc notulam codici Augiensi apposuit, forsan allucinatus'. 'Lost' is the notice's view, not settled
claims.witness: Notitia/scripta ex Cave, PL 68 (liberatus-victor-tunnunensis-primasius-junillus-pl68-lat_migne1866 l.34982-34986, 35021-35031; OCR 'Inieriit', 'duduni', 'Prwdestinali', 'Maliillonius', 'Opussancti', 'Auijuslini', 'Ihrresibus', 'allucinalua')

claims.claim: Pauline commentaries printed under his name ('Commentaria in Epistolas S. Pauli, ex Hieronymi ...'); Bardenhewer counts 'ein ebensolcher Kommentar unter dem Namen des Primasius von Hadrumetum (Migne 68, 413-686)' among the later reworkings of Pelagius's commentary
claims.witness: PL 68 scripta (liberatus-victor-tunnunensis-primasius-junillus-pl68-lat_migne1866 l.34963); Otto Bardenhewer 1924 (bardenhewer_geschichte-altkirchlichen-literatur-band4-augustinus-slice-deu_1924 l.4476-4482; OCR 'Haclrumetum')

claims.claim: Burkitt: 'The chief writers who used Tyconius as their main authority in explaining the Apocalypse were Primasius, Bede, ... and above all Beatus'
claims.witness: F. C. Burkitt 1894 (tyconius_liber-regularum_burkitt1894 l.399-402)

claims.claim: Monceaux: Tyconius's commentary can be largely restored 'grâce aux deux plagiaires qui l'ont le plus systématiquement pillé: l'évêque africain Primasius d'Hadrumète ... et le prêtre espagnol Beatus de Libana'; 'Primasius, évêque influent, chef de parti, auteur célèbre en son temps, avait des prétentions au beau style'
claims.witness: Paul Monceaux 1920 (monceaux_histoire-litteraire-afrique-chretienne-tome5_1920 l.10330-10339; OCR 'IIadrumète')

claims.claim: Mesnage: 'Primasius a été un des évêques les plus savants de son temps'
claims.witness: Joseph Mesnage 1912 (mesnage_afrique-chretienne-eveches-ruines-antiques-fra_1912 l.10268-10278)

claims.claim: Migne heads his works 'PRIMASIUS ADRUMETANUS EPISCOPUS'
claims.witness: PL 68 (liberatus-victor-tunnunensis-primasius-junillus-pl68-lat_migne1866 l.34926-34929)

claims.claim: He is a WHO participant of the council, part 'African bishop; signed Vigilius's Constitutum'
claims.witness: Council profile entry (Council-Profiles/era3/second-council-of-constantinople-553.entry.json, l.198)

contested_claims.claim: Victor of Tunnuna's account of his surrender for the primacy, persecution of his former side, condemnation and unhappy death
contested_claims.sides: Victor of Tunnuna tells it, as a defender of the Three Chapters (chronica-minora-2_marcellinus-victor-tunnunensis-biclaro-isidore-mgh-aa-11-lat_mommsen1894 l.19115-19121). Heinrich Kihn: how much is true is hard to decide, and it is not free of party coloring (kihn_theodor-von-mopsuestia-junilius-africanus-instituta-lat-deu_1880 l.12698-12701). No independent second witness.

contested_claims.claim: The monastery he was sent to
contested_claims.sides: Acoemetensi, the Sleepless monks: Mommsen's correction (chronica-minora-2_marcellinus-victor-tunnunensis-biclaro-isidore-mgh-aa-11-lat_mommsen1894 l.19115; 'aquimetensis libri', l.19164). Kihn names no monastery (kihn_theodor-von-mopsuestia-junilius-africanus-instituta-lat-deu_1880 l.12675, 12690). Aquimetensis: Migne's text (liberatus-victor-tunnunensis-primasius-junillus-pl68-lat_migne1866 l.74709-74710).

contested_claims.claim: His see
contested_claims.sides: Hadrumetum (Justinianopolis): his own signature (collectio-avellana_epistulae-imperatorum-pontificum-v1-lat_guenther1895 l.24165-24168), Cassiodorus (cassiodorus_opera-institutiones-pl70-lat_migne1847 l.60691). Utica: Gagny's dedication (liberatus-victor-tunnunensis-primasius-junillus-pl68-lat_migne1866 l.35122), Trithemius, rejected by Baronius per Kihn (kihn_theodor-von-mopsuestia-junilius-africanus-instituta-lat-deu_1880 l.12523-12525).

contested_claims.claim: The Pauline commentaries under his name
contested_claims.sides: His: Migne's edition and Cave's list (liberatus-victor-tunnunensis-primasius-junillus-pl68-lat_migne1866 l.34963). A later reworking of Pelagius's commentary under his name: Bardenhewer (bardenhewer_geschichte-altkirchlichen-literatur-band4-augustinus-slice-deu_1924 l.4476-4482).

contested_claims.claim: Whether his work on heresies is lost, or survives as the Praedestinatus
contested_claims.sides: Lost: the notice from Cave that Migne prints, 'Interiit jam dudum opus istud' (liberatus-victor-tunnunensis-primasius-junillus-pl68-lat_migne1866 l.34982-34983; OCR 'Inieriit', 'duduni', 'isiud'), which ends by doubting the Reichenau title: 'quisquis hanc notulam codici Augiensi apposuit, forsan allucinatus' (l.35030-35031; OCR 'allucinalua'). His: the title in the old Reichenau manuscript Mabillon saw, 'Opus sancti Primasii, discipuli Augustini, de Haeresibus numero XC' (l.35027-35028; OCR 'Opussancti', 'Auijuslini', 'Ihrresibus'), toward which the same notice first leans: 'Longe potiori jure tribuendi videntur Primasio nostro' (l.35020-35021; OCR 'videnlur', 'noslro'). Other authors the notice reports for the Praedestinatus: Hyginus, under whose name Hincmar of Reims cites it, which the notice calls a plain error (l.34999-35002); Sirmond's Arnobius the Younger (l.35002-35004); and Piccinardus's Vincentius (l.35004-35020).
